ranked_methods.name: Short-horizon candle reversal with taker-flow gate (fade the last candle or candles)
ranked_methods.hypothesis: On liquid crypto pairs, the sign of the last 5-15 minute candle tends to reverse. Liquidity providers who absorb aggressive taker flow are paid through a partial reversal, so the effect is concentrated after bars whose move agreed with the taker imbalance and carried high flow intensity. The information sits mostly in the sign of recent returns rather than their size, fades within hours, and is essentially absent in US equities and ETFs. Merged from the academic 'short_horizon_sign_reversal' and the microstructure 'flow_driven_reversal'.
ranked_methods.formula: Uses the common notation (CN, methodology item 1). Input series: x_t = rt_t when ret_def='cc'; when ret_def='oc', x_t = clip(ln(C_t/O_t)/(S_slot(t)*sigma_{t-1}), -10, 10). Kernel: u_t = sum_{k=0..K-1} lam^k*phi(x_{t-k}) / sum_{k=0..K-1} lam^k. phi(x) = sign(x) with phi(0)=0 when mode='sign'; phi(x) = clip(x,-2,2)/2 when mode='mag'. So |u_t| <= 1. Flow gate, used only when taker_buy_base_volume exists (otherwise G_t = 1): fd_t = 1 if sign(i_t) == sign(r_t) and |i_t| >= theta, else 0; intensity_t = |i_t|*min(vs_t, 3), where vs_t = V_t/medV_slot(t); G_t = w0 + (1-w0)*fd_t*min(1, intensity_t/I_ref), so G_t is in [0,1]. Score: score_t = -clip(kappa*u_t*G_t, -1, 1). Warm-up: mode='sign' needs K+1 bars. mode='mag' and ret_def='oc' need sigma (>= 288 bars) and S (S=1 until 10 completed days). Before that, score_t = 0. Keep the baseline (K=1, mode='sign', kappa=1, w0=1), which reduces to score_t = -sign(r_t), as a permanent reference expert. Do not use the BVC proxy for i_t here: BVC imbalance is a monotone function of r_t, so the gate adds nothing.
ranked_methods.evidence: Kitron & Wengrowicz (arXiv 2608.21888, Aug 2026; existence and abstract confirmed via RePEc listing) ran a strictly out-of-sample walk-forward on 15-minute candles. 90% of 183 Binance USDT pairs showed significant directional reversal, against 2.7% of 187 US stocks and ETFs. Lag-1 autocorrelation is about 0 on the majors, but betting against the previous candle captures most of the effect. The class-mean AUC gap versus equities is +0.031 (95% CI +0.027 to +0.035), or +0.011 under the most conservative accounting. About 70% of bars are 'flow-driven' (the move agrees with 2*TB/V-1), and the reversal concentrates in those bars and grows with flow intensity. The effect decays to no skill within hours. A third-party critique (GitHub issue, confirmed by fetch) reports AUC 0.527 for one lag and 0.531 for a 12-lag kernel, about 1.3 bps gross per trade, no depth, latency or adverse-selection costs, volume ranking done after the sample ended (survivor tilt), and that the authors disclose running an automated trading system on variants of the model. Supporting evidence: De Nicola (Ledger 2021) finds significant negative first-order BTC autocorrelation at 1-6 hours, with larger moves reversing more. arXiv 2003.13517 finds significant 5-minute autocorrelation on major crypto markets, negative at small scales and partly bid-ask bounce. Heston, Korajczyk & Sadka (2010) attribute reversal at horizons under an hour to temporary liquidity imbalances plus bounce.
ranked_methods.caveats: The headline evidence is at 15 minutes, not 5. Expect a 5-minute AUC of about 0.50-0.53 on BTC/ETH (hit rate about 51-53%). The gross edge of about 1.3 bps is below any 2-10 bps taker round trip, so this is an ensemble feature, a maker-side quote skew, or a high-|score| filter, not a standalone taker strategy. Part of the measured last-trade reversal is bid-ask bounce that cannot be captured by crossing the spread; check robustness with the skip-one-bar target. Expect about zero for SPY/ES and let the ensemble weight go to 0 there. The sign can weaken or flip in strong trend regimes; regime_conditioned_autocorr models that, and this method should not be flipped by the ensemble. The method is highly collinear with regime_conditioned_autocorr, large_move_reversal and short_oscillator_reversion, so treat them as one family with a capped combined weight. Full texts could not be fetched (egress blocked).

ranked_methods.name: Noise-area intraday momentum with VWAP trailing stop (Zarattini-Aziz-Barbon)
ranked_methods.hypothesis: Moves that stay inside a time-of-day-specific noise band around the session open are noise. A close outside the band, confirmed by VWAP, signals a supply/demand imbalance that tends to persist for the rest of the session. VWAP and the band act as a trailing stop. The vwap_only variant reduces to 'long above session VWAP, short below'. Merged from the academic 'noise_area_breakout' and the practitioner 'noise_area_vwap_trend'.
ranked_methods.formula: Uses CN. Session start bar s0 = anchor(t). j = t - s0 is the 0-based slot within the session. O_s = O_{s0}. Cprev = C_{s0-1}: the previous RTH close for equities; for crypto this is the previous bar's close, about O_s, so there is no gap. Noise width: sig_j = mean over the D most recent completed sessions d of |C_{s0_d+j}/O_{s0_d} - 1|. At least 0.7*D sessions must have slot j, otherwise score_t = 0. UB_t = max(O_s, Cprev)*(1 + mult*sig_j); LB_t = min(O_s, Cprev)*(1 - mult*sig_j). VWAP_t is the session VWAP from s0 to t (CN). State pos in {-1,0,+1}, reset to 0 at s0. variant='noise_area', processed in this order each bar. (1) Stops, every bar: if pos=+1 and C_t < (vwap_stop ? max(UB_t, VWAP_t) : UB_t), set pos=0; if pos=-1 and C_t > (vwap_stop ? min(LB_t, VWAP_t) : LB_t), set pos=0. (2) Entries and flips, only on decision bars where (j+1) mod check_every == 0: if C_t > UB_t and C_t > VWAP_t, set pos=+1; else if C_t < LB_t and C_t < VWAP_t, set pos=-1. (3) Excursion: e_t = max(0, (pos=+1 ? C_t - UB_t : LB_t - C_t))/(O_s*sig_j). score_t = pos_t*clip(m_min + g*e_t, 0, 1). variant='vwap_only': for j >= 6, pos_t = sign(C_t - VWAP_t) if |C_t - VWAP_t| > deadzone_atr*ATR14_t, else pos_{t-1}; score_t = pos_t*min(1, |C_t - VWAP_t|/ATR14_t). Equities: score_t = 0 on the last RTH bar, because t+1 is the next session's gap bar. Warm-up: score 0 until D completed sessions exist.
ranked_methods.evidence: Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon, 'Beat the Market' (SFI WP 24-97; details confirmed via search): on SPY from 2007 to early 2024, a 14-day noise area with multiplier 1, a gap adjustment, half-hourly entry checks and VWAP/band trailing stops returned 1,985% in total net of costs (19.6% a year, Sharpe 1.33). It placed 4th in the Quantpedia Awards 2025. Zarattini & Aziz, 'VWAP: The Holy Grail' (QQQ, 1-minute bars, 2018-2023): Sharpe 2.1 and max drawdown 9.4%, but public QuantConnect replications came out much lower. Concretum's BTC intraday trend ensemble (2018-2025) had a gross Sharpe of about 1.6, against just under 0.8 for vol-targeted buy and hold. Academic support for intraday continuation: Gao et al. (JFE 2018), Li, Sakkas & Urquhart (JFM 2022), and Shen, Urquhart & Wang (Financial Review 2022, BTC).
ranked_methods.caveats: The published results are strategy PnL with positive skew from trailing stops on trend days, not next-bar sign accuracy. The per-bar hit rate may be only about 50-51% even where the strategy pays, so evaluate with return-weighted and cost-adjusted edge, not raw accuracy. It is the most fee-robust method here because positions persist for many bars and turnover is low. Evidence is medium for SPY/ES/QQQ. For crypto, the 00:00 UTC open is conventional rather than structural, so treat it as low confidence and let the anchor be tuned (us_open_ny is the most defensible). Replications are lower than published figures, and the effect may decay after publication. It overlaps with intraday_tsmom_session_end and trend_state_momentum (trend family cap) and is anti-correlated with vwap_band_reversion.

ranked_methods.name: End-of-session intraday time-series momentum (first or rest-of-session return predicts the last window)
ranked_methods.hypothesis: Late in the session, the return so far (or the first half-hour return, measured from the previous close) predicts the final 30-60 minutes. Proposed causes: gamma hedging by short-gamma option and leveraged-ETF dealers, infrequent rebalancing, and late-informed trading. The effect is strongest on volatile, high-volume days. Crypto needs a defined session anchor.
ranked_methods.formula: Uses CN. Session [A, E): 'equity_rth' = 09:30-16:00 America/New_York. This covers SPY and ES cash hours, and for crypto it applies the same NY clock to crypto prices on weekdays only. '00:00UTC' = [00:00, 24:00) UTC (crypto). Active iff bar t+1 opens in [E - L_min, E), i.e. t+1 is one of the last L_min/5 bars; otherwise score_t = 0. P0 = close of the last bar ending at A (equities: the previous session's final RTH bar, so the overnight gap is included). Raw predictor: mode='first': R_t = ln(C at A+F_min / P0). mode='rest': R_t = ln(C_t/P0). mode='gao2' (equity_rth only): R1 = ln(C at A+30m / P0) and R12 = ln(C at E-L_min / C at E-L_min-30m). Normalizer: recompute the same quantity at the same clock time in each of the previous 20 sessions; sR = sqrt(mean of squares), with at least 10 sessions required, otherwise score 0. z_t = R_t/sR, or for gao2 z_t = (R1/sR1 + R12/sR12)/sqrt(2). Vol boost: RV_t = sqrt(sum of r_s^2 over session bars in [A, t], excluding the first bar of the session). hv_t = 1 if RV_t exceeds the median RV at the same slot over the previous 20 sessions, else 0. Score: score_t = tanh(c*z_t)*(1 + delta*hv_t)/(1 + delta).
ranked_methods.evidence: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (JFE 2018), SPY 1993-2013: the first half-hour return (measured from the previous close) predicts the last half-hour. In-sample R2 is about 1.6-2% (4.3% in the financial crisis) and out-of-sample R2 is up to 1.8%, or 2.7% with the 12th half-hour added. The effect is stronger on volatile, high-volume and macro-news days. A 2012-2014 replication found correlation 0.12 and R2 0.014. Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens (JFE 2021): across 60+ futures from 1974 to 2020, the rest-of-day return predicts the last 30 minutes, linked to short-gamma hedging. Li, Sakkas & Urquhart (JFM 2022): the effect holds out of sample in 16 developed markets, stronger when liquidity is low and volatility high. Shen, Urquhart & Wang (Financial Review 2022): BTC first half-hour predicts last half-hour when sessions are defined by volume. Wen et al. (NAJEF 2022): both intraday momentum and reversal in crypto.
ranked_methods.caveats: Coverage is only 6-12 bars per session. A 30-minute correlation of about 0.12 spread over six 5-minute bars implies a per-bar correlation of about 0.05, or a hit rate of about 51.5%. The effect reportedly weakened after 2013. Medium confidence for SPY/ES; low for crypto, where the anchor is arbitrary and Shen et al.'s exact volume-based session definition could not be verified (full text blocked). For ES, use the 16:00 ET cash close, not the 17:00 ET Globex break. Because R is identical across the active window in mode 'first', the six active bars are not independent observations.

ranked_methods.name: Regime-conditioned adaptive autocorrelation (volatility, volume and liquidity regimes; LeBaron, Campbell-Grossman-Wang, Nagel)
ranked_methods.hypothesis: Whether the next bar continues or reverses the last one depends on the regime. Autocorrelation becomes more negative when expected volatility is high (LeBaron), when volume is liquidity-driven (Campbell-Grossman-Wang), and when liquidity is scarce (Nagel, Amihud). It also differs by session and between weekdays and weekends. Estimating the lag-1 coefficient per regime bin with shrinkage lets the data choose momentum or reversal. Merged from the academic 'regime_conditioned_autocorr', the microstructure 'volume_surprise_reversal' (its CGW/LMSW volume gate becomes the volume-tercile bins) and 'liquidity_regime_reversal' (its vol-ratio and Amihud gates become the vol-ratio and illiquidity bins).
ranked_methods.formula: Uses CN. Regime features at t, from bars <= t. Tercile cutpoints (33rd and 67th percentiles) are recomputed once a day from the trailing W_days. vol: vol_feat='level' uses sigma_t; vol_feat='ratio' uses VR_t = sqrt(mean_{k<12} pk_{t-k}/S_slot(t-k)^2) / sqrt(mean_{k<2016} pk_{t-k}/S_slot(t-k)^2). volume: VS_t = (ln(1+V_t) - med)/(1.4826*MAD), where med and MAD are taken over ln(1+V) at slot(t) in the last 20 completed days. illiq: A_t = mean_{k<12} |r_{t-k}|/(C_{t-k}*max(V_{t-k}, Vfloor)), with Vfloor = 1st percentile of V over W_days. session (crypto, assigned in this order): US if 09:30 <= NY time < 16:00; Asia if 00:00 <= UTC < 07:00; EU if UTC >= 07:00 and NY time < 09:30; otherwise Late. Session (equities): open = first 6 bars, close = last 6 bars, otherwise mid. weekend = Saturday/Sunday UTC (crypto only). bin(t) is the tuple of terciles/flags named by 'bins'. Estimation: refit daily at 00:00 UTC, with optional incremental intraday updates of the sums. Use pairs (s, s+1) with s+1 <= t and s in the trailing W_days, binned with the current cutpoints. x_s = clip(rt_s, -cl, cl), y_{s+1} = clip(rt_{s+1}, -cl, cl). mode='slope': rho_b = sum_{bin(s)=b} x_s*y_{s+1} / sum_{bin(s)=b} x_s^2. mode='sign': rho_b = (n_same - n_opp)/n_b, counting only pairs where both returns are nonzero. Shrinkage: rho'_b = rho_b*n_b/(n_b + n0). Prediction: yhat_t = rho'_{bin(t)}*x_t (slope) or rho'_{bin(t)}*sign(r_t) (sign). Score: score_t = tanh(yhat_t/q_ref). Use a fixed q_ref, not a rolling std of yhat, so that when every rho shrinks to 0 the score is also near 0. Warm-up: score 0 until W_days of history and >= 288 bars of sigma exist.
ranked_methods.evidence: LeBaron (J. Business 1992): first-order autocorrelation is inversely related to volatility. Campbell, Grossman & Wang (QJE 1993): autocorrelation falls with volume because liquidity-driven volume is reversed. Llorente, Michaely, Saar & Wang (RFS 2002): hedging-driven moves reverse while speculative ones continue, which is why the sign per bin is left to the data. LeBaron, Pontiff & Bogousslavsky ('A Century of Market Reversals', 2024): expected volatility and anticipated volume drive reversals. Nagel (RFS 2012): returns to short-term reversal (liquidity provision) rise sharply with VIX. Kitron & Wengrowicz: crypto 15-minute reversal scales with taker-flow intensity. arXiv 2003.13517: intraday volatility is positively linked to short-term predictability in crypto. Range estimators: in a 5-crypto HAR study Parkinson beat Garman-Klass and Rogers-Satchell fit worst. Realized-Amihud work reports that intraday illiquidity predicts short-term returns.
ranked_methods.caveats: LeBaron, CGW, LMSW and Nagel are daily or weekly equity results; transfer to 5-minute crypto is plausible but not established. Binning splits the sample: with 9 bins and 60 days (17,280 pairs) each bin has about 1,900 pairs, so the standard error of rho is about 0.023, the same size as the effects. Keep n0 large and prefer one- or two-feature bins. This method nests short_horizon_reversal (one bin, sign mode); cap their combined weight or orthogonalize. It is the only method allowed to output either sign by construction. Volatility and illiquidity regimes are also where spreads and slippage are widest, which may consume any gain. Floor V in Amihud to avoid blow-ups on near-zero-volume bars.

ranked_methods.name: Fixed-share exponentially weighted forecaster on log-loss with a null expert
ranked_methods.hypothesis: Every base method's would-be prediction is observed on every bar, so this is a full-information experts problem. Exponential weights on calibrated log-loss, with eta=1 being a Bayesian mixture, track whichever method is currently best, with regret bounded by ln(K+1) nats. A fixed-share term allows switching across regimes. A null expert (p=0.5) lets the ensemble fall back to no signal. This is the daily-updated ensemble-weighting layer.
ranked_methods.formula: Experts k=1..K are the base scores s_k,t in [-1,1], each at its currently selected parameters. Expert 0 is null, with p_0 = 0.5. Daily calibration at 00:00 UTC, on the trailing 30 days with purging: fit the logistic regression 1{C_{s+1} > C_s} ~ b0 + b1*s_k,s on non-tie bars where s_k,s != 0. a_k = clip(calib_shrink*b1/2, 0, a_max). Set a_k = 0 if the HAC t-stat of b1 is below 1. Methods are switched off, not sign-flipped. Expert probability: p_k,t = 0.5 + 0.5*a_k*s_k,t. Online update at the close of bar t, scoring the predictions made at t-1: skip if C_t == C_{t-1}. Otherwise y = 1{C_t > C_{t-1}}; l_k = -[y*ln p_k,t-1 + (1-y)*ln(1-p_k,t-1)]; v_k = w_k*exp(-eta*l_k); w_k <- (1-alpha_fs)*v_k/sum_j v_j + alpha_fs/(K+1). Optional discounted variant replacing fixed share: L_k <- beta*L_k + l_k, w_k proportional to exp(-eta*L_k), beta = 0.5^(1/(H_days*bars_per_day)). Caps after every update: w_k <= 0.35 for each non-null expert, and the sum per family <= 0.5. Families: reversal (short_horizon_reversal, regime_conditioned_autocorr, large_move_reversal, short_oscillator_reversion, vwap_band_reversion, three_bar_reversal); trend (noise_area_breakout, intraday_tsmom_session_end, trend_state_momentum, ema_ribbon_pullback, opening_range_breakout, compression_breakout); flow (kyle_impact_residual, vpin_gated_flow, trade_size_intensity); seasonal (seasonal_slot_prior). Excess weight moves to the null expert. Initial weights are 1/(K+1). Ensemble: p_t = sum_k w_k*p_k,t. Score: score_t = clip((2*p_t - 1)/a_max, -1, 1).
inputs: base method scores s_k,t in [-1,1] (all causal)
trailing per-expert calibration slopes (refit daily, causal)
ranked_methods.evidence: Hedge (Freund & Schapire 1997) has regret at most sqrt((T/2) ln K). On log-loss with eta=1 it is Vovk's aggregating algorithm or a Bayes mixture, with total regret at most ln(K+1): about 3.0 nats for K=20. Fixed share (Herbster & Warmuth 1998) bounds tracking regret against the best sequence of experts with S switches. For scale, a true 52% expert gains about 0.0008 nats per bar, about 6.9 nats per 30 crypto days, so the regret allowance absorbs about half the edge in a month. Bandit methods (EXP3, Thompson sampling) discard counterfactual information here. Forecast-combination literature (Rapach-Strauss-Zhou RFS 2010; the combination puzzle, Wang et al. 2022) supports shrinking toward equal weights.
ranked_methods.caveats: It needs calibrated experts: an over-confident expert loses to the null expert even with a real 52% edge, which is why the Platt-derived a_k and the clip at a_max exist. Regret is relative to the best expert in hindsight, so it cannot tell skill from luck; promotion of new experts must still pass the online-FDR and deflated-hurdle gates. A convex combination ignores correlation, so with eta >= 1 weight piles onto whichever correlated expert got lucky. Prefer eta 0.25-0.5 plus the family caps. It creates no edge: if all experts are coin flips, it converges to the null expert, which is the correct outcome.

ranked_methods.name: Confidence- and cost-gated selective prediction with adaptive coverage
ranked_methods.hypothesis: Most 5-minute bars have no predictable direction, and fees exceed the expected edge on almost all of them. Abstaining unless the ensemble is confident and its expected move clears round-trip cost raises accuracy on the bars it does predict and is the only route to net profitability. An adaptive threshold holds coverage at a target so statistics remain measurable.
ranked_methods.formula: Inputs: ensemble probability p_t (from hedge_fixed_share_ensemble or online_logistic_stacker), returns r, slots (CN). Expected absolute next move: m_t = EWMA_{half-life = vol_hl bars}(|r_s|/S_slot(s)) at t, times S_slot(t+1). The next slot is known at t. Expected edge: E_t = (2*p_t - 1)*m_t, in log-return units. c_rt = round-trip fee + 2*half-spread + slippage, in log units (10 bps = 0.0010). Gate: g_t = 1 if |p_t - 0.5| >= tau_t AND |E_t| >= c_rt + b, else 0. With hold_rule='same_sign', if g_{t-1}=1 and sign(p_t - 0.5) == sign(p_{t-1} - 0.5), the cost term is waived because the position is held and no new cost is paid, but the tau condition still applies. Score: score_t = g_t*clip((2*p_t - 1)/(2*p_cap - 1), -1, 1). Online coverage control (ACI): tau_{t+1} = clip(tau_t + gamma*(g_t - c_star), 0, 0.1). Daily reset: candidate tau* = the (1 - c_star) quantile of |p - 0.5| over the trailing validation window. Accept it only if, over at least 1,000 validation bars with |p - 0.5| >= tau*, the 95% Clopper-Pearson upper bound on selective error is < 0.5; otherwise keep the previous tau. Never lower c_rt to raise coverage. If realized coverage is below 5% for 5 consecutive days, flag the instrument as 'not tradable at current cost'. Always log the ungated ensemble score separately for accuracy metrics.
ranked_methods.evidence: Chow (1970): the Bayes-optimal reject rule abstains when max(p, 1-p) is below 1 minus the reject cost. Geifman & El-Yaniv (2017): selective-risk guarantees via a threshold chosen with a binomial bound. Gibbs & Candes (2021): the ACI update achieves the long-run target frequency under arbitrary distribution shift. Jaquart et al. (2021): 1-60 minute BTC predictability is profitable before costs and negative after. A 2026 hourly BTC-USDT walk-forward (about 70k hours, 27 folds) found naive sign trading fails at 10 bps, and a cost-threshold filter rescued only some configurations.
ranked_methods.caveats: It helps only if accuracy actually rises with |p - 0.5|; check daily with an accuracy-by-decile table. The cost condition will almost never pass on BTC 5-minute bars at Binance VIP0 spot taker fees (about 15-20 bps round trip) or even 10 bps: with E|r| of about 8-14 bps and p about 0.52, E_t is about 0.3-0.6 bps. That is an honest outcome, so report it rather than tuning around it. Lower coverage slows validation: at 20% coverage, confirming 52% takes about 19,300 bars (about 67 crypto days, about 250 ES RTH days).

ranked_methods.name: Volatility-standardized large-move (drift-burst) reversal
ranked_methods.hypothesis: Extreme, high-volume moves (liquidation cascades, demand for immediacy, overreaction) are partly reversed over the following bars, and more so after negative bursts on heavy volume. Because the trigger is rare and the conditional move is large, the expected reversal in bps can be larger than the unconditional short_horizon_reversal edge, which helps against fees.
ranked_methods.formula: Uses CN. Shock z-score with vol from before the shock window: Z_t = ln(C_t/C_{t-m}) / (sigma_{t-m}*sqrt(sum_{j=0..m-1} S_slot(t-j)^2)). Seasonal volume ratio: v_t = sum_{j<m} V_{t-j} / sum_{j<m} medV_slot(t-j). side_ok = 1 for 'both', 1[Z_t < 0] for 'down_only'. Trigger: trig_t = 1[|Z_t| >= theta]*1[v_t >= v_min]*side_ok. On a trigger, set e = -sign(Z_t)*min(1, 0.25 + (|Z_t| - theta)/theta_w), t0 = t and move0 = |C_t - C_{t-m}|. A new trigger replaces the old event. Score: score_t = e*exp(-(t - t0)/decay_bars) for t0 <= t < t0 + 3*decay_bars; with decay_bars = 0, the score is nonzero only at t = t0. Cancel (score 0 from then on) once the reversal has half-completed: -sign(Z_{t0})*(C_t - C_{t0}) >= 0.5*move0. Otherwise score_t = 0. Warm-up: needs sigma (>= 288 bars) and 20 completed days for medV.
ranked_methods.evidence: Christensen, Oomen & Reno (drift-burst hypothesis): drift bursts occur about weekly across asset classes and are mostly followed by reversion, more strongly after negative bursts on large volume. De Nicola (Ledger 2021): larger BTC moves at 1-4 hours are followed by proportionally stronger reversals. Grant, Wolf & Yu (JBF 2005): highly significant reversals after large opening moves in S&P futures, 1987-2002, that largely lose significance after a bid-ask proxy. Miralles-Quiros & Miralles-Quiros (2022): overreaction after negative hourly BTC shocks, mostly 6-24 hours later. Counter-evidence: Scaillet, Treccani & Trevisan (JFEc 2020) find BTC jumps cluster and cause persistent price changes. A 2026 FRL paper finds BTC intraday reversals around Deribit Friday 08:00 UTC expiries; the gamma-exposure conditioning needs options data and is excluded, and only the timestamp flag could be used.
ranked_methods.caveats: Coverage is about 1-5% of bars, so require at least 100 triggers in the tuning window before trusting its weight. Evidence on the next-5-minute sign is mixed: jumps can continue, cascades can keep going, and most documented reversal plays out over hours. The 'side' and 'v_min' choices double the search space. It is collinear with short_horizon_reversal in mode 'mag' (reversal family cap). Spreads widen in exactly these moments, so slippage is the main cost risk.

ranked_methods.name: Kyle-lambda impact residual (price overshoot versus unpriced taker flow)
ranked_methods.hypothesis: Contemporaneous return is roughly linear in signed order flow (Cont-Kukanov-Stoikov). If price moved more than the flow justifies, the move is an overshoot (temporary impact) and should revert. If it moved less (passive absorption, flow not yet priced), the unpriced flow should continue. The score loads positively on lagged signed flow and negatively on lagged return. It is the only flow-continuation mechanism in the set.
ranked_methods.formula: Uses CN. Per-bar flow: flow_src='taker' (requires TB) gives f_s = i_s. flow_src='clv' (OHLC-only fallback for ES/SPY) gives f_s = ((C_s - L_s) - (H_s - C_s))/(H_s - L_s), or 0 if H_s == L_s. Do not use BVC here: it is a deterministic function of r_s, which makes the residual degenerate. Signed volume: sf_s = f_s*vs_s for impact='linear', or sign(f_s)*sqrt(|f_s|*vs_s) for impact='sqrt', where vs_s = V_s/medV_slot(s). Winsorize sf at the 0.5/99.5 percentiles of the fit window. Fit at bar t by OLS over s in [t-W, t-1]: rt_s = a + lam*sf_s + e_s; sd_e = residual std. Require >= 0.8*W valid bars and lam > 0, otherwise score_t = 0. Aggregate over n bars ending at t: R_n = sum_{k<n} rt_{t-k}; SF_n = sum_{k<n} sf_{t-k}; u_t = R_n - (n*a + lam*SF_n). Score: score_t = -tanh(u_t/(c*sd_e*sqrt(n))). A positive score means price under-reacted to buy flow, or over-shot downward.
ranked_methods.evidence: Cont, Kukanov & Stoikov (JFEc 2014): a linear, stable relation between order-flow imbalance and contemporaneous price change. Silantyev (Digital Finance 2019): on BitMEX XBTUSD, trade-flow imbalance explains contemporaneous moves better than book OFI. Anastasopoulos et al. (J. Financial Markets 2026): crypto order flow alone does not predict returns, but the part of lagged flow orthogonal to lagged returns predicts positively (long-short alpha 0.81% a month, t=5.83, daily/weekly cross-section). Chordia & Subrahmanyam (2004): lagged imbalances relate positively to returns. Kitron & Wengrowicz document the overshoot half (reversal after flow-driven moves) at 15 minutes.
ranked_methods.caveats: The flow-continuation evidence is daily/weekly and cross-sectional; at 5 minutes the reversal leg will probably dominate, which makes it partly collinear with short_horizon_reversal. Kline taker imbalance is trade imbalance, not book OFI (no cancels or limit adds), so much of the CKS explanatory power is lost. Predictive R^2 at 5 minutes is likely well under 1%. The CLV fallback is a crude proxy, so expect near-null results for ES/SPY. Kim & Hansen find baseline imbalance has little predictive association at fine horizons.

ranked_methods.name: Calendar-slot return prior (time-of-day, day-of-week, and quarter-hour turn-of-the-candle)
ranked_methods.hypothesis: Recurring institutional flows, rebalancing, session opens and algorithms that act on completed 15-minute and 1-hour candles leave small, recurring calendar patterns in returns. The trailing mean or sign rate of returns sharing the calendar key of bar t+1 is a weak prior. Merged from the academic 'same_slot_periodicity' and 'quarter_hour_turn_prior'; both estimate a trailing conditional mean keyed on calendar time.
ranked_methods.formula: Uses CN. key(t+1) comes from the open time of bar t+1, which is known at t, in timezone tz. 'slot_day' = slot(t+1). 'slot_week' = (weekday, slot(t+1)). 'hour' = clock hour, pooling all 12 bars of that hour. 'qh_class' (crypto only) = H if the minute-of-hour is 0, Q if it is 15, 30 or 45, O otherwise. For SPY/ES, slots are session slots and qh_class is disabled. Sample: X = {rt_s : s <= t, key(s) == key(t+1), s within the last D_days days}. If split_weekend (crypto), use only days of the same type (Mon-Fri vs Sat-Sun) as t+1, going back until D_days matching days are found. Baseline Y = all rt_s from the same days. stat='mean': z = (mean(X) - demean*mean(Y))/(std(X)/sqrt(n_X)). stat='sign' (nonzero returns only): p = (n_up + 20)/(n + 40); p0 = 0.5 if demean=0, else the same statistic computed on Y; z = (p - p0)/sqrt(p0*(1 - p0)/n). base_t = tanh(z/c) if n_X >= 10, else 0. Optional hour-open flow add-on (crypto, taker data, imb_w > 0): I_h = i of the most recent bar at or before t whose open minute is 00; score_t = clip(base_t + imb_w*tanh(3*I_h), -1, 1). Otherwise score_t = base_t.
ranked_methods.evidence: Heston, Korajczyk & Sadka (JF 2010): stock half-hour returns persist at daily multiples for 40+ trading days, not explained by volume, volatility or spreads. BTC: Quantpedia (2015-2022) finds 21:00-23:00 UTC hours significantly positive. NYDIG (2021) reports day-of-week effects. Baur et al. find BTC time-of-day and day-of-week effects are time-varying and inconsistent. Shanaev, Vasenin & Stepanov (2023, 'turn-of-the-candle'): +0.58 bps per minute at minutes 0/15/30/45 since mid-2020, with other minutes negative on average. K33 confirms the minute pattern after Nov 2021. Hansen, Kim & Kimbrough (JFEc 2024) and Kim & Hansen (arXiv 2607.09426, confirmed via search; Binance futures 2021-2024) find volatility and volume bursts at :00, :15, :30, :45 and every 5 minutes. Hour-open order imbalance forecasts 4-12 hour returns, but average gains at the marks are far below Binance fees (press summary).
ranked_methods.caveats: Slot means of 1-3 bps against 5-minute standard deviations of 10-30 bps need years of data to reach t=2, so with D_days=20 the estimate is mostly noise. Keep c large and expect a small ensemble weight. The quarter-hour effect is +0.58 bps in minute 0 of a 5-minute bar diluted by four slightly negative minutes, so the net bias may be about 0. It is crypto-only, post-2020 and possibly arbitraged. Crypto seasonals are documented as time-varying. Use the America/New_York timezone for US-linked effects so DST is handled. The hour-open imbalance evidence is for 4-12 hours, not the next bar.

ranked_methods.name: Trend-state momentum (SuperTrend or Heikin-Ashi state and flip)
ranked_methods.hypothesis: An ATR trailing band (SuperTrend) or smoothed Heikin-Ashi candles define a short-term trend state. Being on the bullish side, or having just flipped to it, predicts a slight continuation on the next real bar. It provides a 24/7, anchor-free continuation counterweight to the reversal family, with low turnover. Merged from the practitioner 'supertrend' and 'heikin_ashi_trend', which are collinear smoothed-momentum signs.
ranked_methods.formula: variant='supertrend': hl2 = (H+L)/2; ATR = Wilder ATR(atr_len). bUB_t = hl2_t + mult*ATR_t; bLB_t = hl2_t - mult*ATR_t. fUB_t = bUB_t if (bUB_t < fUB_{t-1} or C_{t-1} > fUB_{t-1}) else fUB_{t-1}. fLB_t = bLB_t if (bLB_t > fLB_{t-1} or C_{t-1} < fLB_{t-1}) else fLB_{t-1}. Initialize fUB_0 = bUB_0, fLB_0 = bLB_0, dir_0 = +1. dir_t = +1 if C_t > fUB_{t-1}; -1 if C_t < fLB_{t-1}; else dir_{t-1}. ST_t = fLB_t if dir_t = +1, else fUB_t. mode='state': score_t = dir_t*(beta + (1 - beta)*tanh(|C_t - ST_t|/(mult*ATR_t))). mode='flip': score_t = dir_t*exp(-bars_since_flip_t/flip_decay). variant='heikin_ashi': O',H',L',C' = EMA_{pre_smooth} of O,H,L,C (pre_smooth=1 means raw). HAC_t = (O'+H'+L'+C')/4; HAO_t = (HAO_{t-1} + HAC_{t-1})/2 with HAO_0 = (O'_0 + C'_0)/2; HAH_t = max(H'_t, HAO_t, HAC_t); HAL_t = min(L'_t, HAO_t, HAC_t). color_t = sign(HAC_t - HAO_t); streak_t = number of consecutive same-color bars ending at t. strong_t = 1 if (color=+1 and HAO_t - HAL_t <= 0.05*ATR14_t) or (color=-1 and HAH_t - HAO_t <= 0.05*ATR14_t), else 0. mode='state': score_t = color_t*min(1, streak_t/n_sat)*(0.5 + 0.5*strong_t). mode='flip': score_t = color_t*exp(-(streak_t - 1)/n_sat). Optional htf_confirm='1h': compute the same variant's direction on completed 1-hour bars only, i.e. the last 1h bar that closed at or before the close of bar t; if it disagrees, multiply the score by 0.5. Warm-up: score 0 for the first max(3*atr_len, 50) bars. Always label and evaluate on real closes, never on HA prices.
ranked_methods.evidence: Weak, practitioner-grade evidence. SuperTrend defaults ATR 10 x 3 (Seban). LiberatedStockTrader (4,052 trades, 30 DJIA stocks): 42-43% win rate, unprofitable on daily bars. Quantified Strategies (60+ years of S&P 500): it mainly reduces drawdowns. Unverified TradingView BTC 5-minute claims (55% win rate, profit factor 2.2) are likely overfit. Heikin-Ashi: a tiny 40-day 5-minute test with no costs. TradingView warns that strategies filled at HA prices are unrealistic. HA color is roughly a short EMA-momentum sign. Related: Corbet et al. (2019) find moving-average rules significant on high-frequency BTC; Hudson & Urquhart (2021), testing about 15,000 rules with data-snooping controls, find no out-of-sample predictability for Bitcoin.
ranked_methods.caveats: Expect at most a tiny next-bar edge. It is included mainly as a low-turnover, anchor-free continuation input so the ensemble can down-weight reversal in trends. It whipsaws in ranges and is collinear with ema_ribbon_pullback and noise_area_breakout (trend family cap). The higher-timeframe confirmation must use only completed 1h bars, or it repaints and looks ahead. The recursive HA open depends on initialization, so respect the warm-up.

ranked_methods.name: Online logistic stacker (FTRL-Proximal, shrink-to-prior, forgetting)
ranked_methods.hypothesis: A regularized online logistic regression on the base scores, pulled toward equal weights and slowly forgetting old data, can handle correlated base signals (including negative partial weights) better than a convex expert mixture. It gives slightly better-calibrated probabilities, an expected gain of at most about 0.5-2 percentage points of hit rate. It is deferred only because Hedge plus equal-weight shrinkage covers the first release; use it as the challenger once base-score correlations are observed.
ranked_methods.formula: Features: x_t = [1, s_1,t, ..., s_K,t], with K <= 15. Optionally add 1-2 interactions s_k,t*volz_t, where volz_t is the z-score of the causal EWMA sigma_t against its trailing 30-day distribution. p_t = sigmoid(w . x_t). At the close of bar t, skip ties; otherwise y_t = 1{C_t > C_{t-1}} labels the prediction made at t-1, and g = (p_{t-1} - y_t)*x_{t-1}. FTRL-Proximal is run on u = w - w0, where the prior w0 is 0 for the intercept and 1/K per score; the gradient is unchanged because the loss is evaluated at w = u + w0. Per coordinate i: sig_i = (sqrt(n_i + g_i^2) - sqrt(n_i))/alpha; z_i += g_i - sig_i*u_i; n_i += g_i^2; u_i = 0 if |z_i| <= l1, else u_i = -(z_i - sign(z_i)*l1)/((beta + sqrt(n_i))/alpha + l2). w = clip(u + w0, -2, 2). Forgetting: once a day multiply all n_i and z_i by rho = 0.5^(1/H_days). Score: score_t = clip(c*(2*p_t - 1)/0.2, -1, 1), on the same scale as hedge_fixed_share_ensemble. Daily retune of (alpha, l1, l2, H_days, c) by purged CPCV on the trailing window, moving the live values only part of the way: new = old + 0.25*(chosen - old). Unit test: shifting labels forward by one bar must destroy any edge.
ranked_methods.evidence: FTRL-Proximal with per-coordinate learning rates and elastic-net regularization is the standard streaming logistic regression method (McMahan et al., KDD 2013). Rapach, Strauss & Zhou (RFS 2010): combined forecasts beat the benchmark out of sample where individual predictors fail. The forecast-combination puzzle (Wang et al. 2022 review; arXiv 1505.00475) shows estimated weights often lose to equal weights, hence the shrinkage to the equal-weight prior. Expected gain: a calibrated 52% predictor improves log-loss by only about 0.0008 nats per bar.
ranked_methods.caveats: Collinear scores make individual weights unstable; keep K <= 15, orthogonalize nested pairs (short_horizon_reversal versus regime_conditioned_autocorr), and rely on the l2 pull toward the prior. A half-life under about 10 days (fewer than about 4,000 effective crypto bars) chases noise. A calibration slope <= 0 over the last 3,000 bars means it is anti-predictive and must be rolled back.

ranked_methods.name: Volatility-compression breakout (TTM squeeze, NR4/NR7, inside bar)
ranked_methods.hypothesis: Volatility compression (Bollinger Bands inside Keltner Channels, or the narrowest range in k bars, optionally also an inside bar) is followed by expansion (Crabel). The first close outside the compression box gives a short-lived direction. Merged from the practitioner 'squeeze_breakout' and 'nr_inside_breakout', which share the contraction-to-expansion mechanism. Its more reliable use is as a regime gate.
ranked_methods.formula: Setup detection at bar i. setup='squeeze': mid = SMA_n(C), sd = population std_n(C), BBu/BBl = mid +/- 2*sd; KCm = EMA_n(C), KCu/KCl = KCm +/- k_kc*ATR_n (Wilder). sq_i = (BBu_i < KCu_i) AND (BBl_i > KCl_i). The setup is armed while sq has held for >= min_bars consecutive bars; box = [min L, max H] over those squeeze bars. setup='nr': R_i = H_i - L_i; armed at i if R_i <= min(R_{i-k+1..i}); box = [L_i, H_i]. setup='nr_inside': as 'nr', plus H_i <= H_{i-1} and L_i >= L_{i-1}. An armed setup expires setup_window bars after its last qualifying bar. Breakout: the first t after arming with C_t > boxH + buf*ATR14_t gives dir=+1; C_t < boxL - buf*ATR14_t gives dir=-1. Record t_b and mag = min(1, 0.5 + |C_t - edge|/max(boxH - boxL, 1e-12)), where edge is boxH for up and boxL for down. Score: score_t = dir*mag*exp(-(t - t_b)/decay_bars) for t_b <= t < t_b + 3*decay_bars. Stop (score 0 from then on) if C_t closes back inside the box. Otherwise score_t = 0. Also export sq_t, an NR flag, and the bandwidth percentile ((BBu - BBl)/mid ranked over the trailing 2016 bars) as regime features for the ensemble and other gates. Warm-up: 3*n bars.
ranked_methods.evidence: Practitioner-only and weak. Backtrex BB squeeze on WTI 4h (2016-2026): +73.7% against +94.6% buy and hold, 36% win rate, profit factor 1.21. Quantified Strategies: the squeeze 'doesn't do particularly well' across assets. Crabel (1990) tabulated NR4/NR7 on daily futures and found contraction followed by expansion. Bulkowski: NR7 upward breakouts fail to break even 46% of the time. arXiv 1812.02527: NR patterns are not tradable after costs without additional rules. There is no 5-minute study. Compression reliably predicts a larger next |return| but not its sign.
ranked_methods.caveats: The direction is close to a coin flip, and by the time C_t clears the box part of the move has already happened. Narrow 5-minute bars cluster in dead hours (Asia night, equity lunch) where follow-through is below fees, so consider gating by seasonal volume. Coverage is sparse; require at least 100 breakouts before trusting its weight. It is most valuable as a gate: amplify momentum and breakout signals after a release and dampen reversion.

ranked_methods.name: Short-oscillator and close-location reversion (RSI(2), ConnorsRSI, IBS/CLV, Chaikin money flow) with trend filter
ranked_methods.hypothesis: Extreme readings of very short oscillators, and closes pinned at the bar's high or low (especially on volume), mark temporary aggressor pressure or overextension that partly reverts on the next bar, preferably in the direction of the longer trend. Merged from the practitioner 'connors_short_reversion' and the microstructure 'clv_money_flow_fade'. IBS = (1+CLV)/2, so both are the same close-location fade.
ranked_methods.formula: RSI_n is Wilder's (RMA of gains and losses, alpha = 1/n). Oscillator X_t: variant 'rsi2' uses RSI_2(C)_t. Variant 'crsi': streak_t = +k after k consecutive higher closes, -k after k lower closes, 0 if unchanged; PR_t = percentage of the last 100 one-bar returns below r_t; X_t = (RSI_3(C)_t + RSI_2(streak)_t + PR_t)/3. Oscillator fade: s_osc = clip((Lo - X_t)/Lo, 0, 1) - clip((X_t - (100 - Lo))/Lo, 0, 1). Close location: IBS_t = (C_t - L_t)/(H_t - L_t), set to 0.5 if (H_t - L_t) < min_range_bps*1e-4*C_t; s_loc = clip((band - IBS_t)/band, 0, 1) - clip((IBS_t - (1 - band))/band, 0, 1). Money flow: CLV_s = 2*IBS_s - 1; CMF_t = sum_{k<n} CLV_{t-k}*V_{t-k} / sum_{k<n} V_{t-k}; s_cmf = -tanh(CMF_t/0.5). raw: s_osc for rsi2/crsi; s_loc for 'ibs'; s_cmf for 'cmf'; clip(0.6*s_osc + 0.4*s_loc, -1, 1) for 'rsi2_ibs'. Trend filter: tr_t = sign(C_t - SMA_trend_len(C)_t); w = 1 if raw == 0 or sign(raw) == tr_t, else ctw. Score: score_t = d*raw*w, with d = +1 (fade, default) or -1 (continuation). d = -1 may receive weight only if it wins in at least 70% of walk-forward folds. Warm-up: max(10*n_rsi, 101, trend_len) bars.
ranked_methods.evidence: Connors & Alvarez's RSI(2) and Pagonidis' IBS effect (IBS < 0.2 tends to rise the next day, > 0.8 to fall) are documented on daily US index ETFs and corroborated on country ETFs (arXiv 2306.12434). Intraday transfer is poor: ProRealCode users called 1-minute RSI2 results 'catastrophic'. CLV/CMF next-5-minute evidence is essentially absent. The fade rationale is bounce and temporary imbalance (Heston-Korajczyk-Sadka) plus crypto 15-minute reversal (Kitron & Wengrowicz). Indirect 5-minute support comes from negative short-lag autocorrelation in crypto (arXiv 2003.13517, 2402.11930).
ranked_methods.caveats: The daily edges partly ride index drift and overnight gaps that do not exist on 5-minute crypto. It is strongly collinear with short_horizon_reversal (reversal family cap). The free sign d adds a degree of freedom. Bounce is negligible for BTC/USDT, where the spread is much smaller than the 5-minute range. Expected 1-bar reversion is usually below a 2-10 bps cost.

ranked_methods.name: Session-VWAP standard-deviation band reversion
ranked_methods.hypothesis: When the close is stretched far from session VWAP in volume-weighted standard deviations and the bar shows rejection, price tends to drift back toward VWAP. This is the counterpart of the VWAP-trend rule in noise_area_breakout, and the ensemble decides which applies in each regime.
ranked_methods.formula: Uses CN anchors. Session start s0 is one of: equity_rth; 'utc0' = 00:00 UTC; 'us_open' = 09:30 America/New_York; 'rolling_288' = t-287. TP_i = (H_i+L_i+C_i)/3. Over i in [s0, t]: VWAP_t = sum V_i*TP_i / sum V_i; sd_t = sqrt(max(sum V_i*TP_i^2 / sum V_i - VWAP_t^2, 0)); sd*_t = max(sd_t, 0.25*ATR14_t). If t - s0 + 1 < min_session_bars, score_t = 0. z_t = (C_t - VWAP_t)/sd*_t. base_t = -sign(z_t)*clip((|z_t| - k_entry)/1.0, 0, 1). If require_rejection and z_t > 0: keep base_t only if H_t >= VWAP_t + k_entry*sd*_t and the upper-wick fraction (H_t - max(O_t, C_t))/(H_t - L_t) >= 0.4; mirror this for z_t < 0 with the lower wick; otherwise base_t = 0. Trend damping: slope_t = (VWAP_t - VWAP_{t-6})/ATR14_t (requires t-6 >= s0, else slope = 0). If sign(slope_t) == sign(z_t), base_t = base_t/(1 + lambda_trend*|slope_t|). score_t = clip(base_t, -1, 1).
ranked_methods.evidence: Practitioner evidence only, mixed to negative. Backtrex VWAP 2-sigma fade on DAX 15-minute bars (2016-2026): -98.6% against +137.5% buy and hold, profit factor 0.64. A TradingView XLE 5-minute script had a 69% win rate yet still lagged buy and hold. Zarattini & Aziz find the opposite rule (VWAP trend) profitable on QQQ. Indirect support comes from negative short-lag autocorrelation in crypto.
ranked_methods.caveats: High win rate with negative skew: it keeps losing on trend days. Coverage is a few percent of bars. The crypto anchor is arbitrary, and a rolling VWAP drops the benchmark rationale. A 1-2 bar reversion of a 2-sigma 5-minute stretch is often below cost. It is anti-correlated with noise_area_breakout, which helps diversification but means the regime weighting must be learned.

ranked_methods.name: Opening-range breakout at session opens with relative-volume gate
ranked_methods.hypothesis: The first 5-60 minutes after a session open set a range. Its direction, or a later close outside it, tends to continue, especially when opening-range volume is high relative to its own history (the single-instrument analogue of 'stocks in play').
ranked_methods.formula: Anchor a: equity_rth 09:30 ET; crypto 'utc0' 00:00 UTC, 'eu_open' 08:00 Europe/London, or 'us_open' 09:30 America/New_York. All anchors are DST-aware. The OR window is bars [a, a+or_bars-1]: ORH = max H, ORL = min L, ORV = sum V. RVOL = ORV/mean(ORV over the previous 14 sessions at the same anchor). Before the OR completes, score_t = 0. variant='direction': at e = a+or_bars-1, dir = sign(C_e - O_a) if |C_e - O_a| > 0.05*ATR14_e, else 0; t0 = e. variant='breakout': the first t in (e, a+48] with C_t > ORH gives dir=+1, or with C_t < ORL gives dir=-1; t0 = t. Stops: 'or_opposite' stops a long if C_t < ORL and a short if C_t > ORH. 'atr_frac' stops a long if C_t < C_t0 - atr_frac*ATRd14, mirrored for shorts, where ATRd14 = mean session true range over the previous 14 sessions. After a stop, dir = 0 for the rest of the session. g = use_rvol ? clip((RVOL - rvol_min)/(2.0 - rvol_min), 0, 1) : 1. score_t = dir*g*exp(-(t - t0)/decay_bars) while active; 0 after a stop, and 0 on the last bar of an equity session.
ranked_methods.evidence: Zarattini & Aziz (SSRN 4416622), 5-minute ORB on QQQ: about 24% hit rate and +0.13R per trade, with commissions but no spread or slippage and no out-of-sample test. An independent five-index replication found gross results reproduce but net returns are about zero. Zarattini, Barbon & Aziz: on 7,000+ stocks, 'stocks in play' with RVOL >= 100% returned a Sharpe of 2.81 net. Holmberg, Lonnbark & Lundstrom (FRL 2013): crude-oil ORB returns significantly above a fair game, varying strongly with volatility state. There is no rigorous crypto study.
ranked_methods.caveats: The index ORB edge appears to vanish net of realistic costs, and most of the documented edge is single-stock news RVOL. Next-bar accuracy is a poor metric here (about 24% trade hit rate). Coverage is one setup per anchor per day. Anchors must be exact under DST. Overlaps with noise_area_breakout and intraday_tsmom_session_end.

ranked_methods.name: VPIN toxicity-gated short-horizon signed flow
ranked_methods.hypothesis: When VPIN (how one-sided recent volume is) is high, the most recent signed flow is more persistent or more toxic, so it should carry more weight; when VPIN is low, flow is noise. VPIN is a magnitude/regime variable, so it gates signed flow, and the continuation-versus-fade sign is learned.
ranked_methods.formula: Uses CN. Buy volume: Vb_t = TB_t when taker data exist. Otherwise BVC: Vb_t = V_t*F((C_t - C_{t-1})/sd_288(dC)), where sd_288 is the trailing std of close changes over 288 bars and F is the normal CDF or a Student-t CDF with nu=0.25 (ELO 2016). Vs_t = V_t - Vb_t. Bar-time VPIN: VPIN_t = sum_{k<n}|Vb - Vs|_{t-k} / sum_{k<n} V_{t-k}. Short imbalance: OI_t = sum_{k<m}(Vb - Vs)_{t-k} / sum_{k<m} V_{t-k}. Gate: g_t = clip((pctrank_L(VPIN_t) - p0)/(1 - p0), 0, 1), where pctrank is over the trailing L bars ending at t. Score: score_t = mode*g_t*tanh(OI_t/c), with mode = +1 (continuation) or -1 (fade). Score 0 if sum V = 0 or before L bars of history.
ranked_methods.evidence: Easley, O'Hara, Yang & Zhang (2024): VPIN and Roll measures for BTC/ETH have own- and cross-market predictive power for price dynamics, mainly volatility, liquidity and higher moments rather than return sign. A Coinbase/Bitstamp study (2015-2018) finds VPIN predicts BTC crash risk. Andersen & Bondarenko: VPIN is mechanically tied to volume and volatility, with no incremental volatility forecasting power after controls, and depends on classification. Chakrabarty et al.: the tick rule and Lee-Ready beat BVC on equities. A practitioner BTC test found about a 1.4x lift and no warning before a large drop.
ranked_methods.caveats: There is no direct evidence that VPIN predicts the next 5-minute sign. Its best use is as a confidence multiplier or meta-feature for other signals; report its marginal AUC over the ungated signal. The free 'mode' sign must be stable in at least 70% of folds. Bar-time VPIN only approximates volume-time VPIN. With BVC, OI is a function of returns, so it is nearly redundant with the reversal family.

ranked_methods.name: Trade-size versus trade-count conditioned direction
ranked_methods.hypothesis: Binance klines report number_of_trades, so average trade size is V/N. Bars with unusually large average trade size more likely carry informed flow, so the move continues (LMSW). Bars driven by bursts of many small trades carry transient algorithmic or retail pressure, so the move reverses.
ranked_methods.formula: Uses CN. Crypto only; disabled when number_of_trades is missing. ATS_t = V_t/max(NT_t, 1). With seasonal=true: zA_t = (ln ATS_t - med)/(1.4826*MAD), where med and MAD are over ln ATS at slot(t) in the last L/288 days; zN_t likewise for ln(max(NT_t, 1)). With seasonal=false: mean and std over the trailing L bars. Score: score_t = sign(r_t)*tanh(|rt_t|/kappa)*tanh(a*zA_t - b*zN_t). A positive bracket means continuation of bar t's direction; a negative bracket means reversal. Exclude a=b=0 from the grid.
ranked_methods.evidence: Indirect. Jones, Kaul & Lipson (RFS 1994): the number of trades, not their size, drives volatility. Ane & Geman (JF 2000): trade count is a better stochastic clock. LMSW (RFS 2002): informed-trade returns continue and hedging-trade returns reverse. Kim & Hansen (2026): crypto bursts at 1-, 5- and 15-minute marks are algorithmic (trade-size roundness drops), and baseline imbalance has little predictive association at fine horizons. In US stocks, the trade-size-bucketed imbalance relation flipped sign after 2000.
ranked_methods.caveats: The mapping from trade size to informedness is speculative. Large players split orders, and Binance trade counts reflect matching-engine aggregation, so values are venue-specific. It is unavailable for ES/SPY OHLCV feeds. The expected effect is at the edge of detectability.

ranked_methods.name: EMA-ribbon pullback / Raschke Holy Grail continuation
ranked_methods.hypothesis: In an established short-term trend (fully stacked EMA ribbon, or ADX > 30), a pullback to a mid-ribbon EMA followed by a bar resuming the trend marks a continuation entry; the next bars favor the trend.
ranked_methods.formula: E_k,t = EMA_k(C)_t for ribbon [k_1 < ... < k_m]. Alignment: A_t = (1/(m-1))*sum_{i=1..m-1} sign(E_{k_i,t} - E_{k_{i+1},t}), in [-1,1]. variant='ribbon', long trigger at t: A_t == 1 AND there exists i in [t - touch_window, t-1] with L_i <= E_pull,i + tol*ATR14_i AND C_t > E_{k_1,t} AND C_t > H_{t-1}. The short trigger mirrors this (A_t == -1, H_i >= E_pull,i - tol*ATR14_i, C_t < E_{k_1,t}, C_t < L_{t-1}). On a trigger: t0 = t, dir = sign(A_t), mag = 1. variant='holy_grail': require ADX14_t >= adx_min, dir = sign(+DI14 - -DI14), E_pull = EMA20, mag = min(1, ADX14_t/50), with the same touch and resume rules. Score: score_t = dir*mag*exp(-(t - t0)/decay_bars) while dir*(C_t - E_pull,t) > 0 and t - t0 < 3*decay_bars; otherwise 0. Warm-up: 3*k_m bars.
ranked_methods.evidence: Rules come from Raschke & Connors, 'Street Smarts' (1995). Ribbon pullbacks are common TradingView tools with no rigorous published backtests. Corbet et al. (2019) find MA rules significant on high-frequency BTC; Hudson & Urquhart (2021) find no out-of-sample predictability for Bitcoin after data-snooping controls.
ranked_methods.caveats: Anecdotal evidence. It is collinear with trend_state_momentum, has many parameters (high overfit risk), and is sparse. Because the trigger already requires a bar moving in the trend direction, the residual next-bar edge is small.

ranked_methods.name: Three-bar reversal pattern
ranked_methods.hypothesis: Two bars in one direction, then a bar that makes the middle bar the swing extreme and closes beyond the prior bar's high or low, signal exhaustion and a short reversal of the prior swing, especially at an N-bar extreme. On t+1 this is a continuation of bar t's direction.
ranked_methods.formula: Bullish at t: C_{t-2} < O_{t-2} AND C_{t-1} < O_{t-1} AND L_{t-1} < min(L_{t-2}, L_t) AND C_t > O_t AND C_t > ref, where ref = H_{t-1} ('prev_high') or H_{t-2} ('first_high'). All three bars must have H > L. Bearish mirrors this: two up bars, H_{t-1} > max(H_{t-2}, H_t), C_t < O_t, C_t < L_{t-1} (or L_{t-2}). If require_location, bullish requires L_{t-1} == min(L over [t-loc+1, t]) and bearish requires H_{t-1} == max(H over the same window). If vol_confirm, V_t > V_{t-1}. On a pattern: dir = +/-1, t0 = t, mag = min(1, 0.5 + |C_t - ref|/(gamma_atr*ATR14_t)). Score: score_t = dir*mag*exp(-(t - t0)/decay_bars) for t0 <= t < t0 + 3*decay_bars. Set to 0 if a newer opposite pattern appears, or if C_t closes beyond the pattern extreme (below L_{t0-1} for bullish, above H_{t0-1} for bearish). Otherwise score_t = 0.
ranked_methods.evidence: Bulkowski ('Are Three-Bar Patterns Reliable For Stocks', S&C 2000) covers daily bars only. Marshall, Young & Rose (28 candlestick signals, DJIA 1992-2002, bootstrap): 'candlestick technical analysis does not have value'. Lo, Mamaysky & Wang (JF 2000): some kernel-detected daily patterns carry modest incremental information. Nothing rigorous exists at 5 minutes.
ranked_methods.caveats: Probably the weakest method. Because bar t already moved strongly in the signal direction, short-horizon reversal works against it on t+1. Coverage is about 1-3% of bars. Require at least 100 events before giving it weight, and expect the ensemble to assign it about 0.

methodology.topic: 1. Common notation (CN), causality and warm-up conventions used by every formula
methodology.recommendation: Bar t has open time ts_t and values O,H,L,C,V, plus optional TB (taker_buy_base_volume) and NT (number_of_trades). Compute only on closed bars (Binance websocket kline.x == true); bar t's own OHLCV/TB/NT may be used. Label: y_{t+1} = sign(C_{t+1} - C_t). Ties are excluded from scoring and the tie rate is logged; tick size makes ties common: ES 0.25 pt is about 0.4 bps and SPY $0.01 about 0.15 bps. r_t = ln(C_t/C_{t-1}). slot(t): crypto = UTC minute-of-day/5 (0..287); SPY/ES-RTH = minutes since 09:30 America/New_York /5 (0..77). Seasonal vol factor (Andersen-Bollerslev style), recomputed once a day from completed days only: m_k = median |r| in slot k over the last 20 days; S_k = clip(m_k/median_j m_j, 0.2, 5); S_k = 1 until 10 days exist. Base vol: v_t = (1-a)*v_{t-1} + a*(r_t/S_slot(t))^2, with a = 1 - 0.5^(1/288) (1/78 for RTH equities), initialized from the first 288 bars; sigma_t = sqrt(v_t), floored at 0.5*tick/C_t. Standardized return: rt_t = clip(r_t/(S_slot(t)*sigma_{t-1}), -10, 10). Taker imbalance i_t = 2*TB_t/V_t - 1 (0 if V_t = 0); this is the exact aggressor side, so no classification is needed for crypto. medV_k = median V in slot k over the last 20 days; vs_t = V_t/medV_slot(t). Parkinson pk_t = ln(H/L)^2/(4 ln 2). ATR_n = Wilder RMA of true range. Session VWAP uses TP = (H+L+C)/3. Session anchors are shared utilities, DST-aware through the tz database and never fixed UTC offsets: equity_rth 09:30-16:00 America/New_York; 00:00UTC; us_open_ny 09:30 America/New_York; eu_open 08:00 Europe/London. Every rolling statistic, quantile, OLS fit and calibrator uses windows ending at t; any regression that scores bar t is fit on [t-W, t-1]. Higher-timeframe inputs use completed HTF bars only. Missing inputs or an incomplete warm-up give score_t = 0 with covered_t = false, never NaN and never forward-filled. Clip every score to [-1,1] last. Equities: score 0 on the last RTH bar (t+1 is the gap bar), and exclude the first bar of each session from vol estimators. Implement multi-bar setups as causal state machines updated once per bar (score = direction*confidence*exp(-bars_since_trigger/decay)). Add a unit test that shifts inputs forward by one bar: any edge that survives the shift is leakage.

methodology.topic: 2. Seasonal normalization of volume, trade count and volatility
methodology.recommendation: Remove time-of-day effects before z-scoring volume, trade count or range volatility, using per-slot medians and MAD over the trailing 7-28 days (default 20). Crypto shows about 80% excess activity in the first 10 seconds of each hour, 30-50% at :15/:30/:45, smaller bursts every 5 minutes, and session effects at the Asia, EU and US opens. Without seasonal adjustment, 'volume surprise' and 'trade intensity' mostly measure the clock. For ES/SPY use session-relative slots and exclude open and close auction bars. Keep pure clock effects in seasonal_slot_prior, separate from the microstructure signals. Range estimators are for normalization and gating only, never direction. For 24/7 crypto default to Parkinson: open prices are noisy with no auction, and in a 5-crypto study Parkinson beat Garman-Klass while Rogers-Satchell fit worst. For ES/SPY handle gaps with Yang-Zhang or drop gap bars.

methodology.topic: 3. Realistic effect sizes and statistical power
methodology.recommendation: Assume 5-minute direction is 50.0-53% predictable. The best recent out-of-sample crypto evidence (15-minute reversal) is AUC about 0.527-0.531 with about 1.3 bps gross per trade. SPY intraday momentum (30-minute R2 about 1.6-2%) is about 51.5% per 5-minute bar. Treat claims of 54-65% minute-level ML accuracy as optimistic or selection-biased. Hit-rate SE = 0.5/sqrt(N): 1 day (288 bars) 2.9%, 30 days 0.54%, 180 days 0.22%. Bars needed versus 50% (one-sided alpha 0.05, power 0.8): 51% needs 15,454; 52% needs 3,862; 53% needs 1,715; 55% needs 616. Two-sided: 19,620 / 4,903 / 2,178 / 783. Wilson 95% half-width at 52%: plus or minus 3.1 pp at n=1,000, 1.55 pp at 4,000, 0.98 pp at 10,000; the lower bound first clears 50% at about n=2,450. Calendar time: crypto 288 bars/day (52% takes about 13.4 days, 51% about 54 days); ES RTH 78 bars/day (52% about 50 days); divide by coverage for gated methods. A calibrated 52% edge improves log-loss by only about 0.0008 nats per bar. Any skill-estimation window or discount must have effective N at or above the required sample: half-life >= 10 days for crypto at 52%. Daily re-tuning on a few days of data fits noise.

methodology.topic: 4. Evaluation metrics (per method and for the ensemble)
methodology.recommendation: Primary metric: calibrated log-loss (and Brier score) against the p=0.5 baseline; both are proper scoring rules, so use them for all weighting and promotion decisions. Also report: (a) hit rate on non-tie, nonzero-score bars with a Wilson interval and the Pesaran-Timmermann test, which corrects for constant-sign forecasters in drifting markets; (b) AUC; (c) IC = corr(score_t, r_{t+1}); (d) return-weighted accuracy sum(sign(score)*r_{t+1})/sum|r_{t+1}| and the gross edge mean(score*r_{t+1}) in bps, since trend and breakout methods (noise area, ORB at about a 24% trade hit rate) can be profitable with under 50% hits; (e) cost-adjusted edge mean(score_t*r_{t+1}) - c*mean|score_t - score_{t-1}| at c = 2, 5 and 10 bps, and gross bps per trade in the top 5-10% of |score|; (f) coverage for gated or sparse methods, weighting sparse signals by conditional performance times coverage rather than averaging zeros as votes. Checks: a permutation null that shuffles scores against targets within day blocks; a bounce check that re-scores against sign(C_{t+2} - C_t) or skips one bar; and a frozen holdout block (for example a 60-day block reserved each quarter) never touched by daily re-tuning.

methodology.topic: 5. Purged and embargoed walk-forward for the daily re-tune
methodology.recommendation: Outer loop: true walk-forward on a rolling window. Crypto default 60 days (17,280 bars), grid {30, 60, 90, 180}, never below 30. ES/SPY default 120 RTH sessions, grid {60, 120, 250}. Each day, train on [d-W, d-1], score day d, and only then use day d for selection. Inner hyperparameter search: combinatorial purged CV, 6 contiguous groups with 2 test groups (15 splits, 5 paths). Purge training bars whose label interval overlaps a test bar. Embargo max(1% of T, longest feature lookback, 12 bars), and at least 1 day for session-based methods (noise area, tsmom, ORB). Fit every normalizer and calibrator inside the training fold. Use HAC errors (Newey-West lag about 12 bars) or a stationary block bootstrap with 1-day blocks. Keep each method's daily grid at 50 configurations or fewer and search coordinate-wise: tune core parameters first (for example K, lam, mode), then gates. Re-tune at 00:00 UTC for crypto and before the open for equities.

methodology.topic: 6. Overfitting controls on each re-tune: PBO, deflated hurdle, plateau selection, partial moves, sign stability
methodology.recommendation: (a) Keep a permanent trial registry of every configuration and retune ever evaluated; N is cumulative and never resets. (b) Luck hurdle for hit rate: h*(N,n) = 0.5 + 0.5*E[maxZ_N]/sqrt(n), with E[maxZ_N] = (1-g)*InvPhi(1-1/N) + g*InvPhi(1-1/(N*e)) and g = 0.5772. E[maxZ_N] is 1.58 for N=10, 2.53 for N=100 and 3.26 for N=1,000; the best of 100 noise configurations shows 52.8% over 2,000 bars by luck. Promote only if the hit rate exceeds h* and the Wilson lower bound exceeds 0.5. For PnL, require Deflated Sharpe >= 0.95 using per-bar Sharpe, with N = effective trials from correlation clustering (ONC, or clusters at rho > 0.7). (c) PBO via CSCV on a T x N matrix of hourly (12-bar) out-of-sample log-loss gains, S = 16 blocks (12,870 splits; S = 10 gives 252). Accept new parameters only if PBO <= 0.25. If the out-of-sample-on-in-sample slope is <= 0, freeze parameters and update only the ensemble weights. (d) Pick a plateau, not a peak: score each configuration by the mean over itself and its plus-or-minus-1 grid neighbours, and require neighbours to be positive too. (e) Move partially: theta_new = theta_old + 0.25*(theta* - theta_old); integer lookbacks move at most one grid step per day. Keep theta_old unless theta* beats it with a Diebold-Mariano HAC t >= 2, or by more than 2 standard errors versus the literature default. (f) Free sign parameters (d, mode, gamma, side) need the same sign in at least 70% of folds. Sparse methods need at least 100 triggers in the window. (g) Expect BTC to be the hardest market: Hudson & Urquhart found in-sample profitability across about 15,000 rules but none out of sample for BTC.

methodology.topic: 7. Ensemble structure, family caps and calibration
methodology.recommendation: Use full-information exponential weights (hedge_fixed_share_ensemble) as the champion combiner and online_logistic_stacker as the challenger. Do not use bandits (EXP3, Thompson) for weighting; reserve them for scarce live-capital slots, with discount 0.9998 per bar if used. Always include a null expert (p=0.5) and keep an equal-weight ensemble running in shadow. Families: reversal (short_horizon_reversal, regime_conditioned_autocorr, large_move_reversal, short_oscillator_reversion, vwap_band_reversion, three_bar_reversal); trend/breakout (noise_area_breakout, intraday_tsmom_session_end, trend_state_momentum, ema_ribbon_pullback, opening_range_breakout, compression_breakout); flow (kyle_impact_residual, vpin_gated_flow, trade_size_intensity); seasonal. Cap any single method at 0.35 and any family at 0.5; send excess to the null expert. Blend learned and equal weights: w = (1-lambda)*w_learned + lambda/K with lambda = 0.5 (grid 0.25/0.5/0.75), per the forecast-combination puzzle. A new method stays at equal weight until it has 4,000 shadow bars. Keep the pure 'fade last candle' baseline (K=1, sign) as a permanent expert so conditioning gains are measurable. Use VPIN, Kyle lambda, Amihud, squeeze state and ATR percentile as gates or meta-features, keeping a gate only if its marginal AUC over the ungated signal is robustly positive. Gating direction: amplify trend and breakout signals on high-volume, high-volatility sessions and after squeeze releases; favour reversion in quiet hours. Calibrate each method's scores with daily Platt scaling on the trailing 20-30 days (purged), clip ensemble p to [0.40, 0.60], and shrink p' = 0.5 + s*(p - 0.5) with s = 0.5 when the shadow sample is under 4,000 bars. A healthy calibration slope is 0.5-1.5; a slope <= 0 triggers rollback. Switch methods off (a_k = 0) when their trailing skill is negative instead of flipping them; only regime_conditioned_autocorr may output either sign by construction.

methodology.topic: 8. Multiple testing when candidates are added continuously
methodology.recommendation: Treat each new candidate method or configuration as one hypothesis in an online FDR procedure. Get its p-value from a one-sided HAC Diebold-Mariano test (Newey-West lag 12, or a 1-day block bootstrap) comparing ensemble-plus-candidate against the incumbent on log-loss, over a forward shadow period of at least 4,000 bars (about 14 crypto days, about 50 ES RTH days) not used to design it. Accept with LORD++ at q = 0.10, or alpha-investing with initial wealth 0.05 and payout 0.05. Simpler fallback: t >= 3.0 (the Harvey-Liu-Zhu hurdle). For roster-versus-benchmark comparisons use Hansen's SPA or Romano-Wolf StepM. Use the Model Confidence Set to identify methods statistically indistinguishable from the best. Count every candidate, passed or failed, in the deflated-Sharpe N.

methodology.topic: 9. Anytime-valid monitoring and champion/challenger rollback
methodology.recommendation: Re-running a fixed-sample test daily inflates false positives: with true p = 0.5, a daily one-sided 5% z-test falsely flags an edge in 23.6% of runs within 30 days and 30.4% within 90 days. Use a betting martingale K_t = prod(1 + lambda*(2x_i - 1)) over predicted non-tie bars, with lambda = 0.04 for p1 = 0.52 (or adaptive in [0, 0.1] from past data only). Declare an edge when K_t >= 20; Ville's inequality bounds false alarms at 5%. Expect about 3,750 bars to detect a true 52%. Two-sided SPRT for 0.50 versus 0.52 (alpha 0.05, beta 0.2): bounds +2.77 and -1.56, +0.0392 per hit and -0.0408 per miss, about 2,380 bars under H1 and 1,680 under H0. Shadow-run the champion, previous champion, equal weight and null expert, and keep the last 5 good versions. Roll back if any of these fire: (i) DM t < -2.0 versus the previous champion over the trailing 864 bars (10 days for ES RTH); (ii) a Bernoulli CUSUM S_t = max(0, S_{t-1} + miss_t - 0.495) crosses h = 25 (simulated mean time to alarm: about 9,750 bars at a true 52%, 1,990 at 50%, 590 at 47%); (iii) the Wilson upper bound over the last 2,000 predicted bars falls below 0.50; (iv) net drawdown exceeds 3x the backtest's 95th-percentile daily drawdown; (v) the calibration slope over 3,000 bars is <= 0. Ladder: previous champion, then equal weights, then abstain on every bar until the martingale crosses 20 again. ADWIN or Page-Hinkley on per-bar log-loss are drop-in alternatives. Log every rollback as a trial.

methodology.topic: 10. Costs, bid-ask bounce and tradability
methodology.recommendation: Break-even hit rate for a 1-bar round trip with move size independent of correctness: p_be = 0.5 + c/(2*E|r|). Measure E|r| causally per instrument. BTC 5-minute E|r| is about 8-14 bps: at c = 10 bps p_be is about 0.86-1.0 (unreachable); at c = 2 bps it is about 0.57-0.62. Binance spot VIP0 is 0.10% per side (20 bps round trip, 15 with the BNB discount); USD-M futures taker is about 5 bps per side. ES is about 0.5-1 bp round trip against an E|r| of 4-8 bps (p_be about 0.55-0.60). SPY at about 0.2-0.5 bp gives p_be about 0.52-0.55, the only setting where a 52-53% edge could plausibly pay. Every gross edge in this set (about 0.5-1.5 bps per bar) is below taker costs, so no method is a standalone taker signal. Options: (1) maker-only execution or quote skewing on the predicted side, accepting adverse selection; (2) trade only when selective_cost_gate passes (top 5-10% of |score| with expected move above cost); (3) hold through consecutive same-sign predictions and pay only on flips, preferring persistent, low-turnover signals (noise area, trend state); (4) use forecasts to time entries and exits for slower strategies. Charge fees, 2x half-spread and at least 1 tick or 1 bp per side of slippage in every walk-forward, and report net PnL daily. Apply a large haircut to published intraday Sharpes: the 5-minute ORB was gross-only and a five-index replication netted about 0; the QQQ VWAP 'holy grail' Sharpe 2.1 came out much lower in replications. Last-trade closes carry bid-ask bounce that inflates measured reversal; Grant-Wolf-Yu's S&P futures reversals lost most of their significance after a spread proxy.

methodology.topic: 11. Selective prediction with coverage constraints
methodology.recommendation: Predict (for trading) only when |p - 0.5| >= tau_t AND (2p - 1)*E_t|r| >= c_rt + buffer, where E_t|r| is a causal EWMA of |r|/S (24-bar half-life) times S of the next slot. Target coverage c* = 20% (allowed band 10-40%). Set tau daily as the (1 - c*) quantile of |p - 0.5| on validation, then adapt online: tau_{t+1} = tau_t + 0.005*(g_t - c*), clamped to [0, 0.1]. Accept a threshold only if the 95% Clopper-Pearson upper bound on selective error over at least 1,000 selected validation bars is below 0.5 (Geifman-El-Yaniv, delta = 0.05). The coverage target never overrides the cost condition. If coverage stays below 5% for 5 days, flag the instrument as not tradable at its current costs. At 20% coverage, confirming 52% takes about 19,300 bars; below 10% coverage, daily statistics are meaningless. Always log the ungated score for accuracy research.

methodology.topic: 12. Non-stationarity and decay
methodology.recommendation: Expect effects to decay or flip. McLean-Pontiff found anomaly returns 26% lower out of sample and 58% lower after publication. Gao et al.'s first-to-last half-hour effect reportedly weakened after 2013. BTC intraday seasonals are time-varying (Baur et al.). Turn-of-the-candle appeared only in mid-2020. BTC's short-interval Hurst exponent rose from about 0.42 (2019-20) to about 0.49 (2021-22). Order-flow predictability is regime-unstable: in Schmalz's BTC/USDT OFI study the out-of-sample sign flipped twice as the sample grew from 7 to 9 to 17 days. Track rolling 30/90/180-day statistics per method, use forgetting factors with half-lives of 10-60 days (never under 10 for crypto), let weights decay toward zero when the rolling cost-adjusted IC turns negative, and run a CUSUM change detector on each method's per-bar log-loss contribution. Do not hard-code literature parameters as permanent; shrink toward them instead.

methodology.topic: 13. Instrument portability (crypto versus ES/SPY) and session anchors
methodology.recommendation: Crypto: 288 slots a day, 7 days a week, no gaps. Session-based methods (noise area, tsmom, ORB, VWAP) take the anchor as a tunable parameter from {00:00 UTC, eu_open 08:00 London, us_open_ny 09:30 New York}. The US open is the most defensible, because BTC volatility and liquidity peak at major stock-market opens (Eross et al.) and BTC intraday momentum is strongest with volume-defined sessions (Shen et al.). Rolling 288-bar windows are the anchor-free fallback. Calendar flags that need only timestamps are allowed: Binance funding times (00:00/08:00/16:00 UTC) as clock anchors only, since funding rates are not available, and Deribit Friday 08:00 UTC expiry as a candidate event flag; gamma exposure needs options data and is excluded. SPY: 78 RTH slots; handle the gap-containing first bar separately; overnight returns enter tsmom and the noise area through P0/Cprev = previous close. ES: trades about 23 hours, but use cash-session (09:30-16:00 ET) slots for session methods, because the documented effects are tied to the cash session. Instrument expectations: short_horizon_reversal about null for SPY/ES and strongest for crypto (especially alts, where costs are also higher); tsmom and noise area strongest for SPY/ES; seasonal qh_class and trade_size_intensity are crypto-only; kyle_impact_residual and vpin_gated_flow fall back to CLV/BVC proxies and are weak without taker data. number_of_trades is venue-specific (Binance aggregates fills).

methodology.topic: 14. Merge log, exclusions and source provenance
methodology.recommendation: Merges (27 researcher methods became 19): flow_driven_reversal went into short_horizon_reversal (from short_horizon_sign_reversal); noise_area_vwap_trend into noise_area_breakout; volume_surprise_reversal and liquidity_regime_reversal into regime_conditioned_autocorr; same_slot_periodicity and quarter_hour_turn_prior into seasonal_slot_prior; supertrend and heikin_ashi_trend into trend_state_momentum; squeeze_breakout and nr_inside_breakout into compression_breakout; connors_short_reversion and clv_money_flow_fade into short_oscillator_reversion (IBS = (1+CLV)/2). No method required order book, funding, open interest or news. The only excluded inputs were Deribit gamma exposure (options data) and funding rates; their timestamps are kept as calendar flags. Formula fixes: regime_conditioned_autocorr now uses a fixed q_ref so near-zero coefficients cannot be inflated by a rolling std; kyle_impact_residual drops BVC flow (degenerate with returns); short_horizon_reversal disables the BVC gate; tsmom drops the unverifiable 'auto' anchor; large_move_reversal gains an explicit decay and cancel rule; selective_cost_gate uses the next slot's seasonal factor. Provenance: researchers' page fetches to arXiv, SSRN, RePEc and publishers were blocked by the egress proxy, and so were this synthesis's. This synthesis confirmed via search that Kitron & Wengrowicz (arXiv 2608.21888) and Kim & Hansen (arXiv 2607.09426) exist with the summarized findings, fetched the GitHub critique (AUC 0.527/0.531, 1.3 bps gross, post-sample volume ranking, authors disclose operating a trading system on the model), and confirmed the Zarattini-Aziz-Barbon SPY figures (14-day noise area, multiplier 1, 19.6% a year net, Sharpe 1.33). All other effect sizes come from abstracts and snippets. Check exact defaults against the PDFs before relying on them; treat vendor backtests (TradingView, LiberatedStockTrader, Backtrex, Quantified Strategies) as hypothesis sources, not evidence.

methods.name: Short-horizon sign reversal kernel (bet against the last candle(s))
methods.hypothesis: At 5 to 15 minute horizons, liquid crypto pairs show directional mean reversion. Liquidity providers absorb aggressive (taker) flow and are paid through a partial reversal. The signal sits in the signs of recent returns rather than their size, is strongest at the highest frequency and fades within hours. It is close to absent in US equities and ETFs.
methods.formula: Use the common notation (methodology item 1). r_t = ln(C_t/C_{t-1}); rt_t = r_t/(S_slot(t)*sigma_{t-1}). Kernel: u_t = sum_{k=0..K-1} lam^k*phi(rt_{t-k}) / sum_{k=0..K-1} lam^k. phi(x) = sign(x) when mode='sign' (phi(0)=0), or phi(x) = clip(x,-2,2)/2 when mode='mag'. Optional taker gate, used only if taker_buy_base_volume exists and gamma>0: imb_t = 2*TB_t/V_t - 1; a_t = max(0, sign(r_t)*imb_t); g_t = (1+gamma*a_t)/(1+gamma). Without the gate, g_t = 1. Score: score_t = -clip(kappa*u_t*g_t, -1, 1). The case K=1, mode='sign', kappa=1, gamma=0 is the pure rule score_t = -sign(r_t).
methods.evidence: Kitron & Wengrowicz (arXiv 2608.21888, Aug 2026) tested 15-minute candles from 2025-01 to 2026-02 strictly out of sample. 90% of 183 Binance USDT spot pairs showed significant directional reversal, against 2.7% of 187 US stocks and ETFs, and the effect held in every coin-year since 2021. Lag-1 autocorrelation is about zero on the major coins, but simply betting against the previous candle captures most of the effect. The effect is strongest at the highest frequency, decays to no skill within hours, and is concentrated after aggressive taker flow. A third-party critique (GitHub issue) reports AUC 0.527 for one lag and 0.531 for a 12-lag kernel, a gross edge of about 1.3 bps per trade, survivor bias (volume ranked after the sample ended) and no cost or slippage model. De Nicola (Ledger 2021) finds significant negative first-order autocorrelation of BTC returns at 1, 2 and 4 hours, with larger moves reversing more. A separate arXiv study (2003.13517) finds significant autocorrelation at 5 minutes on all major crypto markets it studied, with negative values at small intraday scales partly due to bid-ask bounce.
methods.caveats: Realistic hit rate is about 52-53% (AUC about 0.53), and the gross edge of about 1.3 bps per trade is below 2-10 bps round-trip taker costs, so it is not tradable on its own as a taker strategy. Part of the 5-minute negative autocorrelation in last-trade closes is bid-ask bounce, which cannot be captured by crossing the spread. Expect roughly zero for SPY and ES (2.7% of US names significant). The sign can flip in strong trend regimes, which method 7 handles. The evidence comes from abstracts and summaries; full texts could not be fetched (egress blocked).

methods.name: Volatility-standardized large-move (drift-burst) reversal
methods.hypothesis: Bursts of extreme, high-volume moves (liquidation cascades, demand for immediacy, overreaction) are partly reversed in the following bars. The reversal is said to be stronger after negative bursts with heavy volume.
methods.formula: m-bar shock z-score using vol from before the shock window: Z_t = ln(C_t/C_{t-m}) / (sigma_{t-m} * sqrt(sum_{j=0..m-1} S_slot(t-j)^2)). Seasonal volume ratio: v_t = sum_{j<m} V_{t-j} / sum_{j<m} medV_slot(t-j), where medV_slot is the median volume of that time-of-day slot over the prior 20 days. Trigger: trig_t = 1[|Z_t| >= theta] * 1[v_t >= v_min] * side_ok, where side_ok = 1 for 'both', 1[Z<0] for 'down_only' and 1[Z>0] for 'up_only'. Score: score_t = -sign(Z_t) * min(1, 0.25 + (|Z_t|-theta)/theta_w) * trig_t. Otherwise score_t = 0.
methods.evidence: Christensen, Oomen & Reno (drift burst hypothesis) find that drift bursts happen about once a week across equities, fixed income, FX and commodities. Most are followed by price reversion, and the reversal is stronger for negative bursts with large volume. De Nicola (2021) finds that larger BTC moves at 1 to 4 hour scales are followed by proportionally stronger reversals. Grant, Wolf & Yu (JBF 2005) find highly significant reversals after large opening moves in S&P futures over 1987-2002, but significance falls sharply after a bid-ask cost proxy. Miralles-Quiros & Miralles-Quiros (J. Applied Econ 2022) find overreaction after negative hourly BTC shocks, mostly 6 to 24 hours later. Counter-evidence: Scaillet, Treccani & Trevisan (JFEc 2020; Mt.Gox 2011-2013) find BTC jumps cluster and induce persistent price changes rather than reversals. A 2026 Finance Research Letters paper finds intraday BTC reversals around Deribit option expiries (Fridays 08:00 UTC), strongest when gamma exposure is negative.
methods.caveats: Triggers are rare (about 1-5% of bars), so most bars score 0 and the in-sample hit rate on triggered bars is noisy. Evidence on the next-5-minute sign is mixed: jumps can also continue, and much of the documented reversal plays out over hours, not one bar. Reversal after a liquidation cascade can come only after the cascade finishes, so trading into the fall is costly. Use side asymmetry with care, because it doubles the search space.

methods.name: End-of-session intraday time-series momentum (first or rest-of-session return predicts last window)
methods.hypothesis: Late in the session, the return so far this session (or the first half-hour return) predicts the final half-hour.
