The proposed causes are gamma hedging by option and leveraged-ETF dealers, infrequent rebalancing and late-informed trading. In crypto the analogue uses a defined 24-hour session anchor.
methods.formula: Session definition. SPY or ES: session open is 09:30 America/New_York and close is 16:00. Crypto: anchor A, with session [A, A+24h). Active only if bar t+1 opens within the last L minutes of the session; otherwise score_t = 0. Reference price P0 is the previous session close (equities, includes the overnight gap), or the close of the bar ending at A (crypto). Predictor: mode='first' gives R = ln(C(A+F)/P0), using the close at F minutes after the open; mode='rest' gives R = ln(C_t/P0). Normalizer: sR = sqrt(EWMA over the past 20 sessions of R_session^2), computed with the same mode at the same clock time in prior sessions (causal). Vol boost: hv = 1[realized vol of today's bars so far > median of the same quantity over the prior 20 sessions]. Score: score_t = tanh(c * R/sR) * (1 + delta*hv)/(1 + delta).
methods.evidence: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (JFE 2018): in SPY 1993-2013, the first half-hour return (measured from the previous close) predicts the last half-hour. In-sample R2 is about 1.6-2% (4.3% in the financial crisis), out-of-sample R2 is up to 1.8% (2.7% when the 12th half-hour is added), and the effect is stronger on volatile, high-volume, recession and macro-news days. A 2012-2014 replication found correlation 0.12 and R2 0.014. Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens (JFE 2021): across 60+ futures from 1974 to 2020, the rest-of-day return predicts the last 30 minutes, linked to short-gamma hedging. Li, Sakkas & Urquhart (JFM 2022): intraday time-series momentum holds in 16 developed markets, out of sample, and is stronger when liquidity is low and volatility is high. Shen, Urquhart & Wang (Financial Review 2022): in BTC, using volume as a proxy for trading time, the first half-hour positively predicts the last half-hour, with the most predictability when the first session has the highest volume or volatility. Wen, Bouri, Xu & Zhao (NAJEF 2022) find both intraday momentum and reversal in crypto, built from 5-minute data at hourly granularity.
methods.caveats: Only 6-12 bars per session are non-zero. A 30-minute correlation of about 0.12 spread evenly over six 5-minute bars implies a per-bar correlation of about 0.05, or a hit rate of about 51.5%. Effects have weakened since publication. The crypto session anchor is arbitrary, and I could not verify Shen et al.'s exact volume-based anchor because full texts were blocked. Treat the crypto variant as low confidence and the SPY/ES variant as medium. For ES, use the 16:00 ET cash close rather than the 17:00 ET Globex break.

methods.name: Noise-area breakout (time-of-day volatility band momentum)
methods.hypothesis: Price moves inside a time-of-day-dependent noise band are noise. A break outside the band, measured as distance from the session open, signals a supply/demand imbalance that tends to continue intraday.
methods.formula: tau = minutes since session open (equities: 09:30 ET; crypto: anchor A). O_d = open of the first bar of session d. Band width: sig(tau) = (1/D) * sum_{i=1..D} |C_{d-i}(tau)/O_{d-i} - 1|, using only completed prior sessions. Upper U_t = max(O_d, Cprev_d)*(1 + mult*sig(tau)) and lower L_t = min(O_d, Cprev_d)*(1 - mult*sig(tau)). Cprev_d is the previous session close for equities; for crypto Cprev_d = O_d, so there is no gap. Excursion: e_t = (C_t - U_t)/(O_d*sig(tau)) if C_t > U_t; e_t = (C_t - L_t)/(O_d*sig(tau)) if C_t < L_t; otherwise e_t = 0. VWAP filter (optional): VWAP_t = sum((H+L+C)/3*V)/sum(V) over session bars up to t; if vwap_confirm and sign(C_t - VWAP_t) != sign(e_t), set e_t = 0. Score: score_t = clip(sign(e_t)*0.3 + g*e_t, -1, 1) when e_t != 0, otherwise 0.
methods.evidence: Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon (SFI working paper 24-97, 2024): on SPY 2007 to early 2024, entering trend-following positions when price leaves the 14-day noise area (multiplier 1, gap-adjusted, VWAP or band trailing stops) returned 19.6% a year net of costs, Sharpe 1.33. It placed 4th in the Quantpedia Awards 2025. Concretum (Zarattini, Pagani, Barbon): an ensemble of high-frequency trend models on BTC, 2018-2025, had a gross Sharpe of about 1.6, against just under 0.8 for vol-targeted buy-and-hold. Li, Sakkas & Urquhart and Gao et al. support intraday continuation, especially on high-volatility days.
methods.caveats: The published performance is a trading-strategy result (positive skew from trailing stops and holding to the close), not a next-bar sign result. Per-bar hit rates for trend rules are often at or below 50% while PnL is positive, so score this method with return-weighted accuracy, not raw accuracy. Crypto has no natural open, so the anchor choice is a degree of freedom to validate. The BTC Sharpe is gross of fees. The method overlaps with method 3, so keep their ensemble weights under joint shrinkage.

methods.name: Same-slot return periodicity (time-of-day / day-of-week seasonal prior)
methods.hypothesis: Returns in a given intraday slot carry on at exact multiples of the daily (and weekly) period, because of recurring institutional flows, rebalancing and session effects such as Asia, EU and US opens and the 21:00-23:00 UTC window. The slot's past mean or sign rate is a weak prior for the next bar.
methods.formula: P = period in bars: 288 for crypto daily, 2016 for crypto weekly, or the session-slot index for SPY/ES (same slot in the d-th previous session). Sample: X = {rt_{(t+1) - d*P} : d = 1..D}. Every element has index <= t, so the sample is causal. If pool='hour', add all 12 bars in the same clock hour as bar t+1 on those days. If split_weekend (crypto, daily period), use only past days whose type (Sat/Sun vs weekday) matches bar t+1, going back until D matching days are found. stat='mean': tstat = mean(X)/(std(X)/sqrt(n)), score_t = tanh(tstat/c). stat='sign': p = (#{x>0} + 5)/(#{x != 0} + 10), score_t = tanh((2p-1)*sqrt(n)/c).
methods.evidence: Heston, Korajczyk & Sadka (JF 2010): stock half-hour returns carry on at daily multiples (lags 13, 26, 39, ...) for at least 40 trading days; volume, volatility and spreads do not explain it, and short-term reversal (under an hour) comes from liquidity imbalances and bounce. BTC: Quantpedia (Gemini hourly data 2015-2022) finds the 21:00-23:00 UTC hours have the most significant positive returns. A simple 21:00 to 23:00 long rule gave 40.6% a year with Calmar 1.79, and on weekends the 15:00-21:00 UTC window is stronger. NYDIG (2021) finds day-of-week effects, with outperformance on Fridays and early in the week. Baur, Cahill, Godfrey & Liu: across 15M+ observations on 7 exchanges, time-of-day and day-of-week effects vary over time and are not consistent or persistent, with a higher-Monday-return and lower-weekend-volume pattern. Eross et al. (RIBAF 2019): volatility is highest at the opens of the three major stock markets and liquidity is lowest in the early morning.
methods.caveats: Slot means are tiny next to slot volatility: a slot mean of 1-3 bps against a 5-minute standard deviation of 10-30 bps needs years of data to reach a t-stat of 2. With D=20 the estimate is mostly noise, so keep c large and let the ensemble shrink the weight. Crypto seasonal effects are documented as time-varying (Baur et al.). DST matters: US-linked crypto flows follow New York time, not UTC, so build slots in America/New_York time for US-session effects.

methods.name: Turn-of-the-candle / quarter-hour slot prior
methods.hypothesis: Algorithms that act on newly completed 15-minute and 1-hour candles produce bursts of volume and volatility at minutes :00, :15, :30 and :45. Since 2020, BTC minute returns at these marks have been positive on average and other minutes slightly negative, so the 5-minute bar that starts on a quarter mark gets a small upward prior.
methods.formula: Class of bar t+1 from its open minute-of-hour: 'H' if minute = 0; 'Q' if minute is 15, 30 or 45; 'O' otherwise. Over trailing N days of completed bars, dropping zero-return bars: p_c = (n_up,c + a)/(n_c + 2a) with a=20, and p_all likewise over all bars. z = (p_class(t+1) - p_all)/sqrt(p_all*(1 - p_all)/n_class(t+1)); base_t = tanh(z/c). Optional taker add-on (imb_w > 0, taker data required): I_h = 2*TB/V - 1 of the most recent minute-0 bar at or before t; score_t = clip(base_t + imb_w*tanh(3*I_h), -1, 1). Otherwise score_t = base_t.
methods.evidence: Shanaev, Vasenin & Stepanov (Managerial Finance 2023, 'Turn-of-the-candle effect in bitcoin returns'): returns average +0.58 bps per minute at minutes 0, 15, 30 and 45, and other minutes are negative on average. The effect holds across exchanges and in quantile, TGARCH-M and out-of-sample tests, and it appears from mid-to-late 2020. K33 Research: only 21 of 60 minutes were positive on average after the November 2021 peak, but minutes 0, 15, 30 and 45 were. Hansen, Kim & Kimbrough (JFEc 2024): BTC and ETH show large volatility bursts in the first minute of the hour, medium ones after 15, 30 and 45, and small ones every 5 minutes. Kim & Hansen (arXiv 2607.09426, 2026) link these bursts to algorithmic trading on Binance perpetuals; order imbalance at the hour open forecasts 4-12 hour returns, weaker at finer marks. A press summary of that work says average gains at these boundaries are far below Binance fees.
methods.caveats: In a 5-minute bar, +0.58 bps in minute 0 is diluted by four slightly negative minutes, so the net bias of the bar may be close to zero. It is far below costs, and it is a crypto-only, post-2020 effect that may have been arbitraged since publication. No documented SPY/ES analogue exists; disable it for those instruments or let the weight shrink to 0. Its main use is as a small prior or tie-breaker in the ensemble.

methods.name: Volatility/volume-regime-conditioned adaptive autocorrelation (LeBaron effect)
methods.hypothesis: Whether the next bar continues or reverses the last one depends on the regime. Serial correlation falls (towards reversal) when volatility and expected volume are high, and differs between calm and stressed, weekday and weekend, and Asia, EU and US sessions. Estimating the lag-1 sign or slope separately in each regime bin lets the data pick momentum or reversal.
methods.formula: Regime features at t, computed from data <= t: vp_t = percentile rank of sigma_t over the trailing 30 days (tercile 0/1/2). volp_t = tercile of V_t/medV_slot(t). wk_t = 1 if Saturday or Sunday UTC. sess_t: Asia 00-07 UTC, EU 07-13:30, US 13:30-20, late 20-24 (DST-aware for US). bin(t) = combination selected by 'bins'. Estimation over completed pairs (s, s+1) with s+1 <= t in the trailing W days. mode='slope': rho_b = sum_{bin(s)=b} rt_s*rt_{s+1} / sum_{bin(s)=b} rt_s^2, with rt clipped to [-cl, cl]. mode='sign': rho_b = 2*#{sign(r_s) = sign(r_{s+1})}/n_b - 1. Shrinkage: rho_b' = rho_b * n_b/(n_b + n0). Prediction: yhat_t = rho_{bin(t)}' * clip(rt_t, -cl, cl) for slope, or rho_{bin(t)}' * sign(r_t) for sign. Score: score_t = tanh(yhat_t/q_t), where q_t = std of yhat over the previous 2016 bars.
methods.evidence: LeBaron (J. Business 1992): first-order autocorrelation is inversely related to volatility, strong in calm periods and weak or negative in volatile ones. Campbell, Grossman & Wang (QJE 1993): daily autocorrelation falls with trading volume, because liquidity-driven volume is reversed. LeBaron, Pontiff & Bogousslavsky ('A Century of Market Reversals', 2024): expected volatility strongly drives autocorrelation, autocorrelation is lower on down days, and anticipated volume (not volume shocks) drives reversals. Li, Sakkas & Urquhart and Gao et al.: intraday momentum is stronger when volatility is high or liquidity low, which is the opposite direction at a different horizon; hence the data-driven sign. The arXiv 2003.13517 study reports a positive link between intraday volatility and short-term predictability in crypto. Kitron & Wengrowicz: crypto reversal scales with taker-flow intensity.
methods.caveats: The LeBaron and Campbell-Grossman-Wang results are daily or weekly in equities, so transfer to 5-minute crypto is plausible but not established. Adding bins splits the sample: with 12 bins and 30 days (8,640 bars), each bin holds about 700 pairs, so the standard error of rho is about 0.04, the same size as the effects. Keep n0 large and prefer the coarser bins. This method nests method 1; keep the ensemble from double-counting them (for example, orthogonalize or cap their combined weight).

methodology.topic: 1. Common notation and de-seasonalization (use in all methods)
methodology.recommendation: Index bars by t with timestamp = bar open. Target: y_{t+1} = sign(C_{t+1} - C_t). r_t = ln(C_t/C_{t-1}). slot(t) = 5-minute time-of-day index (0..287 for crypto; for equities, bars since 09:30 ET). Seasonal vol factor (Andersen-Bollerslev style): S_slot = median over the prior 20 days of |r| in that slot, divided by the median of those 288 per-slot medians, recomputed once a day from completed days only. Base vol: sigma_t^2 = EWMA (half-life 288 bars) of (r_s/S_slot(s))^2 for s <= t. Standardized return: rt_t = r_t/(S_slot(t)*sigma_{t-1}). Hansen-Kim-Kimbrough show strong intra-hour volatility bursts (:00, :15, :30, :45, every 5 minutes), so a per-slot factor matters even within the hour. Zero returns: SPY and ES often print C_{t+1} = C_t at tick size (ES 0.25 pt is about 0.4 bps; SPY $0.01 is about 0.15 bps). Drop ties from hit-rate counts and report the tie rate separately.

methodology.topic: 2. Honest effect-size expectations and statistical power
methodology.recommendation: Assume 5-minute direction is about 50.0-53% predictable. The best recent out-of-sample crypto evidence (15m reversal) is AUC about 0.53 with about 1.3 bps gross per trade. In SPY the classic intraday momentum gives a 30-minute R2 of about 1.6-2%, roughly 51.5% per 5-minute bar. Older claims of 55-65% minute-level accuracy from ML (e.g., Akyildirim et al. 2021) should be treated as optimistic. Power: the standard error of the hit rate is 0.5/sqrt(N). One day has 288 bars (SE 2.9%), 30 days 8,640 (SE 0.54%), 180 days 51,840 (SE 0.22%). Telling 51% from 50% at 2 sigma needs about 40k bars (about 140 days of 5-minute crypto data). Daily re-tuning on a few days of data mostly fits noise.

methodology.topic: 3. Evaluation metrics
methodology.recommendation: Score each method and the ensemble on four measures: (a) hit rate on non-tie bars, with the Pesaran-Timmermann test, which corrects for a constant-sign forecaster scoring well in a drifting market; (b) AUC and log-loss of the probability p = 0.5 + 0.5*score*s, with s calibrated; (c) return-weighted accuracy, sum(sign(score)*r_{t+1})/sum|r_{t+1}|, because trend methods (noise area) can have under 50% hits but positive PnL; (d) net PnL after a per-trade cost of 2, 5 and 10 bps, trading only when |score| > threshold. Report coverage (share of bars with score != 0) for gated methods (2, 3, 4).

methodology.topic: 4. Walk-forward design for the daily re-tune
methodology.recommendation: Use long trailing training windows (90-180 days of 5-minute bars) with an expanding or rolling origin. Purge any labels whose bars overlap the test window and leave an embargo of at least 1 day between train and test. Keep the grid small: the grids above total about 30-360 combinations per method, so prefer coordinate-wise search. Pick parameters by median performance over several folds rather than the maximum, and adjust for multiple testing (Deflated Sharpe Ratio, Probability of Backtest Overfitting via CSCV). For ensemble weights, use an online multiplicative-weights or exponentially weighted log-loss update with a slow forgetting factor (half-life of 30-60 days). Shrink towards equal weights or zero, and cap any single method at about 40%. Switch a method off when its trailing 60-day Pesaran-Timmermann z-score is below 0 rather than letting its sign flip. Methods 1 and 7 can flip sign legitimately; others should not.

methodology.topic: 5. Costs, bid-ask bounce and tradability
methodology.recommendation: Gross edges are about 0.5-1.5 bps per 5-minute bar, against 2-10 bps round-trip taker costs, so no single method here is tradable as a taker signal. Grant-Wolf-Yu found index-futures reversals lose most of their significance after a spread proxy; the quarter-hour effect averages far below Binance fees; Kitron et al.'s 1.3 bps is gross. Possible responses: (a) trade only when the ensemble |score| is in the top 5-10% of its distribution; (b) execute as a maker (post on the predicted side), accepting adverse selection; (c) use the forecast to time entries and exits for slower strategies rather than as a standalone. Close-to-close last-trade returns carry bid-ask bounce, which inflates measured 5-minute reversal; without quotes, check robustness by measuring the target as sign(C_{t+2} - C_t) or by skipping one bar.

methodology.topic: 6. Non-stationarity and decay
methodology.recommendation: Expect effects to decay or flip. McLean-Pontiff found anomaly returns 26% lower out of sample and 58% lower after publication. BTC intraday seasonals are time-varying (Baur et al.). The turn-of-the-candle effect only appeared in 2020. BTC's short-interval Hurst exponent rose from about 0.42 (2019-20) to about 0.49 (2021-22), meaning more efficient markets. Track each method's rolling 30/90/180-day statistics, use forgetting factors, and add a regime-break detector (for example, a CUSUM on the method's per-bar log-loss contribution).

methodology.topic: 7. Instrument portability (crypto vs ES/SPY)
methodology.recommendation: Crypto: 288 slots a day, 7 days a week, no gaps. Build US-linked features (US open 09:30 ET, US close 16:00 ET) in America/New_York time so DST is handled; 00:00 UTC (daily candle) and Binance funding times (00:00, 08:00, 16:00 UTC) are natural anchors or extra regime features. Deribit option expiry (Friday 08:00 UTC, settled on a 07:30-08:00 TWAP) is a candidate event flag for reversal. SPY: 78 regular-session slots; treat the first bar after the open, which includes the overnight gap, separately; overnight returns enter method 3 through P0 = previous close. ES: nearly 23 hours a day, but use the cash-session (09:30-16:00 ET) slot index for methods 3-5, since the documented effects are tied to the cash session. Expect method 1 to be about null and method 3 to be the strongest for ES and SPY, and the reverse for crypto.

methodology.topic: 8. Research provenance note
methodology.recommendation: WebFetch to arXiv, SSRN, RePEc, publishers and most blogs was blocked by the egress proxy in this run. All effect sizes above come from search-engine abstracts and summaries plus one GitHub issue that critiques arXiv 2608.21888, not from full-text reading. Before relying on exact defaults, verify the key numbers against the PDFs: Kitron & Wengrowicz AUC and bps, Gao et al. R2, Shanaev et al. 0.58 bps, and the noise-area definition.

methods.name: Flow-driven candle reversal (taker-imbalance-conditioned fade)
methods.hypothesis: In crypto, the sign of a 5-15m candle tends to reverse, and the reversal is concentrated in bars where aggressive taker flow pushed price the same way it moved. This fits liquidity provision being paid for absorbing temporary taker pressure: the book refills within the bar, and the impact of the taker flow partly decays. Direction: fade the last candle, more strongly when the move was flow-driven and intense.
methods.formula: Notation: r_t = ln(C_t/C_{t-1}) (or oc variant r_t = ln(C_t/O_t)). Taker imbalance i_t = 2*TB_t/V_t - 1, with i_t = 0 if V_t = 0. If taker volume is missing (ES/SPY), use the BVC proxy i_t = 2*T_nu(r_t/sd_N(r)) - 1, where T_nu is the Student-t CDF (nu=0.25 per ELO 2016) or Phi. sigma_t = Parkinson vol over the trailing N bars: sqrt(mean_{k<N}[ln(H/L)_{t-k}]^2/(4 ln 2)). medV_t = trailing median of V over N bars (inclusive of t). fd_t = 1 if sign(i_t) == sign(r_t) and |i_t| >= theta, else 0. intensity_t = |i_t| * min(V_t/medV_t, 3). mag_t = tanh(|r_t|/(kappa*sigma_t)). score_t = -sign(r_t) * mag_t * [w0 + (1-w0) * fd_t * min(1, intensity_t/I_ref)]. The score lies in [-1,1]. Setting w0=1 gives the pure 'bet against the previous candle' baseline. All inputs use bars <= t only.
methods.evidence: Kitron & Wengrowicz (arXiv 2608.21888, Aug 2026) ran a strictly out-of-sample walk-forward on 183 Binance USDT spot pairs at 15-min bars. 90% of pairs show significant directional reversal, against 2.7% of 187 US stocks/ETFs. The class-mean out-of-sample AUC gap vs equities is +0.031 (95% CI +0.027 to +0.035), or +0.011 under the most conservative accounting. Lag-1 return autocorrelation is about zero on the majors, but betting against the previous candle captures most of the effect. They use the Binance kline taker imbalance 2*TB/V - 1. About 70% of bars are 'flow-driven' (the sign of the move agrees with the imbalance), the reversal concentrates after flow-driven moves and grows with flow intensity, and the depth a move consumes conditions nothing. The gross edge peaks at about 1.3 bp per trade against a 5 bp round trip. Supporting work: BTC shows significant negative first-order autocorrelation at 1-6h, with larger moves reversing more (Ledger, 'On the Intraday Behavior of Bitcoin'). In equities, short-term reversal is driven by temporary liquidity imbalances lasting under an hour plus bid-ask bounce (Heston, Korajczyk & Sadka 2010).
methods.caveats: This is the best-supported signal in this lens, but the headline evidence is at 15 minutes, not 5. Expect next-5m AUC of only about 0.50-0.53 on BTC/ETH majors, with somewhat more on smaller alts where the cost is also higher. The gross edge (about 1.3 bp) is below even a 5 bp round trip, so it is not tradable taker-to-taker. It is useful as an ensemble feature, as a maker-side quote skew, or with a high |score| threshold. For SPY/ES the cited study finds almost no reversal (2.7% of equities), so the daily weighting should push it toward zero there. The BVC fallback is a noisy classifier. It is highly correlated with methods 4 and 6, so treat them as one cluster in the ensemble.

methods.name: Kyle-lambda impact residual (price overshoot vs. unpriced flow)
methods.hypothesis: Contemporaneous price change is roughly linear in signed order flow (Cont-Kukanov-Stoikov; Silantyev for BTC). Comparing the realized return with the return the flow 'justifies' gives two cases. If price moved more than the flow implies, it is an overshoot (temporary impact or noise) and should revert. If price moved less (passive absorption, so the flow is not yet priced), the remaining flow component should continue. Equivalently, the score loads positively on lagged signed flow and negatively on lagged return.
methods.formula: sf_t = i_t * V_t / Vbar_t, where Vbar_t = trailing mean volume over W bars. In the sqrt variant, sf_t = sign(i_t) * sqrt(|i_t| * V_t / Vbar_t). Estimate lambda_t by rolling OLS over bars s in [t-W, t-1]: r_s = a + lambda*sf_s + e_s. Store sd_e as the residual std of that fit. Aggregate over n bars: R_n = sum_{k<n} r_{t-k}, SF_n = sum_{k<n} sf_{t-k}. u_t = R_n - (a*n + lambda_t*SF_n). score_t = -tanh(u_t/(c * sd_e * sqrt(n))). Positive score means flow exceeded the price response (continue the flow) or the price overshot downward (revert up).
inputs: taker_buy_base_volume (or BVC/CLV-based buy fraction for ES/SPY)
methods.evidence: Cont, Kukanov & Stoikov (J. Fin. Econometrics 2014) find a linear, stable relation between order-flow imbalance and contemporaneous price change, with slope inversely proportional to depth. Silantyev (Digital Finance 2019) finds that on BitMEX XBTUSD, trade-flow imbalance explains contemporaneous price change better than book OFI. Anastasopoulos, Gradojevic, Liu, Maynard & Tsiakas (J. Financial Markets 2026) find crypto order flow on its own is insignificant for predicting returns. The component of lagged order flow uncorrelated with lagged returns, however, has a positive and significant predictive relation with future returns. Their result is at daily/weekly horizons, cross-sectionally, with a long-short alpha of 0.81% (t=5.83). Chordia & Subrahmanyam (2004) report a positive relation between lagged imbalances and returns, driven by autocorrelated imbalances. Kitron & Wengrowicz show the 'price-overshoot' half (reversal after flow-driven moves) at 15m in crypto.
methods.caveats: The positive-flow evidence is at daily/weekly horizons. Applying it at 5 minutes is an extrapolation, and at very short horizons the reversal leg will probably dominate. Kline taker imbalance is trade imbalance only, not book OFI (no cancels or limit adds), so much of the CKS-style explanatory power is lost. The contemporaneous R^2 of flow vs. return is high, but the predictive R^2 at 5m is likely well under 1%. lambda is noisy in thin or quiet periods: floor W, and winsorize sf at +/-5 sd. Fitting on [t-W, t-1] and then scoring t is causal.

methods.name: BVC-VPIN toxicity-gated short-horizon flow
methods.hypothesis: VPIN measures how one-sided recent volume is (flow toxicity). When it is high, informed or one-sided flow dominates, and the most recent signed flow should be more persistent, which favors continuation. When it is low, flow is noise. VPIN is mainly a magnitude/regime variable, so it is used here as a gate on signed flow rather than as a standalone direction signal. The sign (continuation vs. fade) is left to the walk-forward because the crypto 15m evidence points toward fading intense flow.
methods.formula: Buy volume: Vb_t = TB_t if taker data is available, else Vb_t = V_t * T_nu((C_t - C_{t-1})/sd_N(dC)) (bulk volume classification; nu=0.25 per ELO 2016 or the normal CDF per ELO 2012). Vs_t = V_t - Vb_t. Bar-time VPIN approximation: VPIN_t = sum_{k<n}|Vb-Vs|_{t-k} / sum_{k<n} V_{t-k}. The exact version uses equal-volume buckets of size ADV/50 over the last n=50 buckets, filled from bars by prorating volume. OI_t = sum_{k<m}(Vb-Vs)_{t-k} / sum_{k<m} V_{t-k}. g_t = clip((pctrank_L(VPIN_t) - p0)/(1 - p0), 0, 1), where pctrank uses only the trailing L bars. score_t = mode * g_t * tanh(OI_t/c), with mode in {+1 continuation, -1 fade}.
methods.evidence: Easley, O'Hara, Yang & Zhang (2024) find that Roll measures and VPIN for BTC/ETH have own- and cross-market predictive power for crypto 'price dynamics', stable through crypto winter. The targets in this research line (see also Easley, Lopez de Prado, O'Hara & Zhang, 'Microstructure in the Machine Age', RFS 2021) are mainly volatility, liquidity and higher-moment dynamics, not return sign. A study of Coinbase/Bitstamp data from 2015-2018 (J. Futures & Options 2020) finds VPIN predicts BTC crash risk (NCSKEW and DUVOL) under both tick-rule and BVC classification. Andersen & Bondarenko show VPIN is mechanically correlated with volume and volatility, has no incremental power for future volatility after controls, and depends heavily on the classification method. Chakrabarty et al. find the tick rule and Lee-Ready beat BVC on equities. A practitioner test over 60 days of BTC found only about a 1.4x lift with no warning before a large drop.
methods.caveats: There is no direct evidence that VPIN predicts the sign of the next 5m return. Its documented value is for crashes, jumps and volatility, so its best use is as a gate or confidence multiplier for other signals. Leaving the sign 'mode' free gives the optimizer an extra degree of freedom, so require the chosen sign to be stable across the majority of walk-forward folds before giving it weight. With 5m bars, bar-time VPIN is only a coarse approximation of volume-time VPIN. For crypto, prefer exact taker volume to BVC: Binance reports the aggressor side, so there is no reason to estimate it.

methods.name: Volume-surprise-conditioned reversal (Campbell-Grossman-Wang / Llorente et al.)
methods.hypothesis: Price moves on abnormally high volume that come from non-informational liquidity demand get absorbed by liquidity providers who are paid via subsequent reversal, so return autocorrelation becomes more negative with volume. Where volume reflects informed or speculative trading, high-volume moves continue instead. This method needs only OHLCV, so it also works for ES/SPY.
methods.formula: lv_t = ln(V_t + 1). Seasonal baseline: mu_t = median of lv at the same time-of-day slot over the last D days (288 slots per day for 24/7 crypto, session slots for ES/SPY). s_t = 1.4826 * MAD over the same set. Trailing alternative: mean and std over N bars. VS_t = (lv_t - mu_t)/s_t. z_t = r_t/sigma_t, with sigma_t = Parkinson vol over N bars. score_t = clip( -tanh(z_t/kappa) * (beta0 + gamma*tanh(VS_t)), -1, 1). gamma > 0 means high volume amplifies reversal (CGW). gamma < 0 with |gamma| > beta0 means high-volume bars continue (LMSW informed regime).
methods.evidence: Campbell, Grossman & Wang (QJE 1993) find first-order return autocorrelation for indices and large stocks declines (becomes more negative) with volume. Their model has market makers paid for absorbing non-informational pressure. Llorente, Michaely, Saar & Wang (RFS 2002) find returns from risk-sharing trades reverse while those from speculative/informed trades continue, and the volume-autocorrelation relation varies with information asymmetry. Kitron & Wengrowicz find crypto 15m reversal grows with flow intensity, which is consistent with the CGW sign (gamma > 0) in crypto. Nagel (RFS 2012) shows reversal (liquidity-provision) returns rise sharply with volatility (VIX). Kim & Hansen document volume/volatility bursts at :00/:15/:30/:45, which is why the volume baseline should be seasonal.
methods.caveats: CGW and LMSW are daily-horizon equity studies, so applying them at 5m is extrapolation. In crypto the evidence points to gamma >= 0, but the sign may flip in news-driven regimes such as macro prints for ES/SPY. Without seasonal adjustment, VS mostly picks up time-of-day and the US-open effect. The effect is small: expect it to add at most about 0.005 AUC on top of method 1. For SPY/ES, 5m reversal is weak and bid-ask bounce is about 0.2-1 bp, so the effect is likely below cost.

methods.name: Close-location / money-flow fade (CLV, Chaikin money flow)
methods.hypothesis: Where the close sits within the bar's range is a crude proxy for who traded last and for intrabar buy-pressure share. A close pinned at the high, especially on high volume, often marks temporary aggressor pressure or the last print being at the ask, which tends to give back (bid-ask bounce, temporary impact). The default direction is to fade it. The opposite 'close-strength continuation' reading exists in TA lore, so the sign is tested. For ES/SPY, (1+CLV)/2 also serves as an OHLC-only buy-volume fraction, an alternative to BVC.
methods.formula: CLV_t = ((C_t - L_t) - (H_t - C_t))/(H_t - L_t), set to 0 if H_t == L_t or if (H_t - L_t)/C_t < min_range_bps*1e-4. CMF_t = sum_{k<n} CLV_{t-k}*V_{t-k} / sum_{k<n} V_{t-k}, which lies in [-1,1]. score_t = d * tanh(CMF_t/c), with default d = -1 (fade) and d = +1 for continuation.
methods.evidence: Direct academic evidence that CLV predicts the next 5m return sign is weak to absent. CLV is a standard TA quantity: Williams/Chaikin, used in the accumulation/distribution line. The fade rationale comes from bid-ask bounce and temporary liquidity imbalances, which Heston, Korajczyk & Sadka (2010) identify as drivers of very short-horizon reversal, and from the crypto 15m reversal results (Kitron & Wengrowicz). Including it lets the walk-forward test a cheap OHLC-only intrabar-pressure proxy for markets without taker volume.
methods.caveats: This is a weak, largely untested hypothesis. Bounce is negligible for BTC/USDT, where the spread is much smaller than the 5m range, and matters more on thin alts. Doji and tiny-range bars produce noisy CLV, hence the min_range filter. Strongly collinear with sign(C-O) and with method 1. Give it a low prior weight and drop it if the fold-sign test fails.

methods.name: Range-volatility and liquidity-regime-scaled multi-bar reversal (Parkinson/GK/RS + Amihud)
methods.hypothesis: Reversal is the return to liquidity provision, and that return is larger when liquidity is scarce: short-term vol is high relative to its norm, or price impact per dollar (Amihud) is elevated. Normalizing an n-bar move by an efficient range-based volatility estimate, then scaling the fade by a liquidity/volatility regime gate, should improve on a raw reversal. Range estimators are used only for normalization and gating. On their own they carry no directional information.
methods.formula: Per-bar variance estimators: Parkinson p_t = [ln(H/L)]^2/(4 ln 2). Garman-Klass gk_t = 0.5[ln(H/L)]^2 - (2 ln 2 - 1)[ln(C/O)]^2. Rogers-Satchell rs_t = ln(H/C)ln(H/O) + ln(L/C)ln(L/O). sigma_X(M) = sqrt(mean_{k<M} x_{t-k}). z_t = ln(C_t/C_{t-n})/(sigma_est(N)*sqrt(n)). Gate options: vol_ratio g_t = sigma_est(M)/sigma_est(N). amihud_ratio g_t = A_t(M)/median_L(A(M)), with A_t(M) = mean_{k<M} |r_{t-k}|/(C_{t-k}*V_{t-k}). none: g_t = 1. G_t = clip((g_t - 1)/(g_hi - 1), 0, 1). mult_t = m0 + (1 - m0)*G_t. score_t = -tanh(z_t/kappa) * mult_t.
methods.evidence: Nagel (RFS 2012) finds expected returns and Sharpe ratios of short-term reversal (liquidity provision) are strongly time-varying, rising sharply with VIX. In BTC, negative autoregressive coefficients are significant up to about 6h, and larger moves revert more (Ledger). Kitron & Wengrowicz find the crypto 15m reversal scales with flow intensity. A study of range-based estimators in a HAR framework on 5 cryptos finds Parkinson beats Garman-Klass (in-sample R^2 11-27%) and Rogers-Satchell fits worst. The authors attribute this to noisy opens in continuously traded crypto with no opening auction. Jones, Kaul & Lipson (1994) show the volatility-volume link runs through the number of trades. Realized-Amihud work reports that intraday illiquidity predicts short-term returns.
methods.caveats: Volatility and illiquidity predict the magnitude of moves well but not their direction. Any gain here comes only from better-timed reversal, and it is strongly correlated with methods 1 and 4. High-vol regimes are also where costs (wider spreads, slippage) are highest, which may eat the improvement. For ES/SPY, exclude the first bar of the session and session-gap bars from range estimators, or use Yang-Zhang across sessions. Amihud on 5m bars with near-zero volume blows up, so floor V and winsorize.

methods.name: Trade-size vs. trade-count conditioned direction
methods.hypothesis: Binance klines report number_of_trades, so average trade size is V/N. Bars with unusually large average trade size more likely carry institutional or informed flow, and their move should continue (LMSW 'speculative trades continue'). Bars whose activity comes from a burst of many small trades (algorithmic slicing, retail frenzy, clock-time bursts) carry more transient pressure and should reverse.
methods.formula: ATS_t = V_t/max(N_t,1). zA_t = (ln ATS_t - mu_A)/sd_A and zN_t = (ln N_t - mu_N)/sd_N, each computed over the trailing L bars. With seasonal=true they are computed per time-of-day slot over the last L/288 days. z_r = r_t/sigma_t (Parkinson over 288 bars). score_t = sign(r_t) * tanh(|z_r|/kappa) * tanh(a*zA_t - b*zN_t). A positive bracket means continuation of bar t's direction, a negative bracket means reversal.
methods.evidence: The evidence here is indirect. Jones, Kaul & Lipson (RFS 1994) find it is the number of transactions, not their size, that drives volatility. Ané & Geman (JF 2000) show trade count is a better stochastic clock than volume. Llorente et al. (RFS 2002) find informed/speculative trade-driven returns continue and hedging-driven returns reverse. Kim & Hansen (arXiv 2607.09426) show crypto bursts at 1-, 5- and 15-minute marks are algorithmic (trade-size roundness drops) and that baseline order imbalance has little predictive association at fine horizons. For US stocks, the trade-size-bucketed imbalance relation with future returns flipped sign after 2000. Trade size is not a stable 'informed' marker.
methods.caveats: This is a speculative mapping from trade size to informedness. In crypto, large players split orders, so ATS reflects matching-engine artifacts and bot behavior more than intent. The interaction depends on the venue: Binance counts aggregated fills, and the count differs from Binance.US and Coinbase. It is not available for ES/SPY OHLCV feeds, so the ensemble should skip it when number_of_trades is missing. Expected effect is at the edge of detectability.

methodology.topic: Causal construction of order-flow features from klines
methodology.recommendation: Use only closed klines: on the Binance websocket, wait for kline.x == true. At close t, TB_t, V_t, N_t and OHLC_t are all known, so features may include bar t. All rolling statistics (means, medians, quantiles, OLS fits, seasonal baselines) must use windows ending at t, and regressions used to score t should be fit on [t-W, t-1]. Define taker imbalance as i_t = 2*TB_t/V_t - 1 (exact aggressor side; no classification needed in crypto). For instruments without taker volume (ES, SPY), substitute bulk volume classification, buy fraction = T_nu((C_t - C_{t-1})/sd), with nu=0.25 (ELO 2016) or the normal CDF, or the CLV proxy (1+CLV)/2. Treat both as noisy: BVC accuracy depends on context, and Chakrabarty et al. find the tick rule and Lee-Ready beat BVC on equities.

methodology.topic: What direction to expect at 5m (sign priors)
methodology.recommendation: Encode these priors and let the walk-forward confirm or override them. (a) Contemporaneous: flow and return are strongly positively related (CKS, Silantyev), so same-bar flow is already priced and is not a forecast. (b) Next bar: fade the bar's move, more strongly when the move was taker-driven and intense (Kitron & Wengrowicz). (c) Flow that is not reflected in price (residual to return) has a positive sign, but the evidence is at daily/weekly horizons (Anastasopoulos et al.). (d) Unconditional lagged imbalance is near zero at fine horizons (Kim & Hansen: baseline and 1-minute imbalance have little predictive association; quarter-hour opening imbalance predicts 4-12h, not 5m). (e) Order-flow signs are long-memory (Lillo-Farmer), but liquidity adjusts so returns stay nearly white. Persistence of flow therefore does not imply persistence of returns.

methodology.topic: Evaluation metric and realistic effect sizes
methodology.recommendation: Score each method by out-of-sample AUC and hit rate on sign(C_{t+1} - C_t), not by R^2, and by gross bp per trade at several |score| thresholds. Realistic targets: AUC 0.505-0.53 for crypto majors at 5m. Kitron & Wengrowicz get a crypto-vs-equity AUC gap of only +0.011 to +0.031 at 15m, with a gross edge of about 1.3 bp against a 5 bp round trip. In Albers et al., microstructure features explain 10-37% of BTC 500ms returns, but that edge decays within seconds and does not carry to 5m bars. Use a permutation null (shuffle score vs. target within day blocks) and a frozen holdout untouched by the daily re-tuning.

methodology.topic: Instability and overfitting guards for the daily re-tune
methodology.recommendation: Order-flow predictability is regime-unstable. In Schmalz's BTC/USDT OFI study, the out-of-sample sign flipped twice as the sample grew from 7 to 9 to 17 days, though OFI plus AR(1) combined beat either alone. So: (1) use trailing windows of at least 30-60 days for re-tuning; (2) require the sign of a method's out-of-sample edge to agree in at least 70% of walk-forward folds before it gets non-zero weight; (3) shrink ensemble weights toward zero, e.g. exponentially-weighted log-loss with a ridge prior; (4) cap how far parameters can move per day; (5) limit the effective grid size and apply a deflated-Sharpe or Romano-Wolf-style multiple-testing haircut, because grids with free sign parameters (mode, d, gamma) add degrees of freedom.

methodology.topic: Seasonality normalization of volume, trade count and volatility
methodology.recommendation: Before z-scoring volume, trade count or range volatility, remove time-of-day effects with per-slot medians over the trailing 7-28 days. Crypto has 80% excess activity in the first 10 seconds of each hour and 30-50% at :15/:30/:45, plus US/EU session effects. Without this, 'volume surprise' and 'trade intensity' mostly measure the clock. For ES/SPY, use session-relative slots and exclude open and close auction bars. Keep pure clock effects (turn-of-candle, quarter-hour) in a separate seasonality module so they are not mixed into the microstructure signals.

methodology.topic: Range-based volatility estimator choice
methodology.recommendation: Use range estimators for normalization and regime gating only. They carry no information about direction. For 24/7 crypto, default to Parkinson: open prices are noisy with no opening auction, and in a 5-crypto study Parkinson outperformed Garman-Klass while Rogers-Satchell fit worst. Keep GK and RS in the grid. For ES/SPY, handle overnight and session gaps (Yang-Zhang, or drop gap bars). Floor sigma at a small multiple of the tick size divided by price to avoid divide-by-near-zero on quiet bars.

methodology.topic: Role of VPIN, Kyle lambda and Amihud: gates, not direction signals
methodology.recommendation: Use VPIN, Kyle lambda and Amihud mainly as multipliers or gates on directional signals, or as meta-features for the ensemble weighting. Their documented predictive content is for volatility, crash/jump risk and liquidity (Easley-O'Hara-Yang-Zhang 2024; the Coinbase/Bitstamp crash study). Andersen & Bondarenko show VPIN is largely a function of volume and volatility with no incremental power after controls. Report each gate's marginal AUC contribution over the ungated signal, and drop the gate if that contribution is not robustly positive.

methodology.topic: Costs and execution: when the edge survives
methodology.recommendation: Assume the reversal and flow signals here are below a taker round trip (2-10 bps per the task). The best-measured one is about 1.3 bp gross at 15m against 5 bp of cost. Monetization options: (1) maker-only execution or quote skewing, where the reversal signal says which side to rest on; (2) trade only in the top 5-10% of |ensemble score| and verify that bp per trade in that tail exceeds the full cost; (3) use the signals as filters or tie-breakers for other strategies rather than as standalone entries. Track net-of-cost P&L in the daily report, not just accuracy.

methodology.topic: Ensemble structure
methodology.recommendation: Methods 1, 4, 5 and 6 are all reversal-family signals and will be highly correlated. Group them into one cluster, weight within the cluster, then combine with the flow-continuation cluster (methods 2 and 3) and the trade-size method (7). Give method 1 with w0=1 (pure 'fade last candle') a permanent baseline slot, so the system can always tell whether the order-flow conditioning adds anything beyond it. Kitron & Wengrowicz find the sign of the last candle carries most of the effect.

methods.name: VWAP standard-deviation band reversion
methods.hypothesis: When the 5m close is stretched far from the session VWAP, measured in volume-weighted standard deviations, and the bar shows rejection, price tends to drift back toward VWAP on the next bar. This is the common 'fade the 2-sigma VWAP band' scalp. The opposite, trend-following VWAP rule is covered in noise_area_vwap_trend, and walk-forward should decide which one holds in each regime.
methods.formula: Session start s(t) depends on anchor: equities use the 09:30 America/New_York RTH open; crypto uses 00:00 UTC (anchor='utc0'), the US cash open (13:30 UTC in summer, 14:30 UTC in winter; anchor='us_open'), or a rolling window of the last 288 bars (anchor='rolling_288'). TP_i=(H_i+L_i+C_i)/3. Over i in [s(t),t]: VWAP_t = sum(V_i*TP_i)/sum(V_i); sigma_t = sqrt(max(sum(V_i*TP_i^2)/sum(V_i) - VWAP_t^2, 0)); sigma*_t = max(sigma_t, 0.25*ATR14_t), where ATR14 is Wilder RMA of true range. If (t - s(t) + 1) < min_session_bars, score=0. z_t = (C_t - VWAP_t)/sigma*_t. base_t = -sign(z_t) * clip((|z_t| - k_entry)/k_span, 0, 1). If require_rejection is true and z_t>0, keep base_t only if H_t >= VWAP_t + k_entry*sigma*_t and the upper-wick fraction (H_t - max(O_t,C_t))/(H_t - L_t) >= 0.4; otherwise set it to 0. Mirror this for z_t<0 using the lower wick. Trend damping: slope_t = (VWAP_t - VWAP_{t-6})/ATR14_t. If sign(slope_t)==sign(z_t) (fading with the VWAP drift against you), multiply base_t by 1/(1 + lambda_trend*|slope_t|). score_t = clip(base_t, -1, 1). All inputs use bars <= t.
methods.evidence: Practitioner evidence only, and it is mixed to negative. A third-party test of a VWAP 2-sigma band fade on DAX 15m from 2016 to 2026 returned -98.6% against +137.5% for buy and hold, with profit factor 0.64 (backtrex). A TradingView 5m XLE VWAP-SD reversion script reported 69% winning trades but still lagged buy and hold (7.3% vs 10.5%). The academic support is indirect. High-frequency BTC returns show significant autocorrelation at 5m (arXiv 2003.13517) and anti-correlation at very short lags (Tang et al., arXiv 2402.11930), which is consistent with some short-horizon reversion. However, Zarattini and Aziz find the opposite (VWAP trend-following) is profitable on QQQ. Expected next-bar hit rate conditional on |z|>2 is at best around 51-53%, and coverage is low (a few percent of bars).
methods.caveats: The win rate looks good, but the payoff is negatively skewed: on trend days the band fade keeps losing, as the DAX result shows. The trend damping and the counterpart vwap_trend signal exist to soften this. The anchor for 24/7 crypto is arbitrary. A rolling VWAP removes the anchor problem but also removes the 'institutional benchmark' rationale. The sigma floor is needed early in the session, when the band is degenerate. At 2-10 bps round-trip cost, a 1-2 bar reversion of a 2-sigma 5m stretch is often smaller than cost on low-vol days, so trade only when the expected move clearly exceeds cost.

methods.name: Noise-area intraday momentum with VWAP trailing stop (Zarattini/Aziz/Barbon)
methods.hypothesis: Moves that leave the time-of-day-specific 'noise area' around the session open signal demand/supply imbalance that tends to persist for the rest of the session. VWAP works as a trailing stop. With vwap_only, the rule reduces to the 'long above VWAP, short below' QQQ system.
methods.formula: Session start s(t): equities 09:30 ET; crypto 00:00 UTC or the US cash open. O_s is the open of the first session bar. Cprev is the close of the last bar before the session (for crypto, essentially O_s). Slot j = t - s(t). For each of the previous D completed sessions d: move_d(j) = |C_{s_d+j}/O_{s_d} - 1|. sigma_j = mean_d move_d(j), using completed sessions only. UB_t = max(O_s, Cprev)*(1 + noise_mult*sigma_j); LB_t = min(O_s, Cprev)*(1 - noise_mult*sigma_j). VWAP_t is the session VWAP with TP=(H+L+C)/3. State pos is in {-1,0,+1} and resets to 0 at session start. Entries (and direct flips) are allowed only on decision bars where (t - s(t) + 1) mod check_every == 0: if C_t > UB_t and C_t > VWAP_t then pos=+1; if C_t < LB_t and C_t < VWAP_t then pos=-1. Stops are checked every bar. A long exits (pos=0) if C_t < (vwap_stop ? max(UB_t, VWAP_t) : UB_t). A short exits if C_t > (vwap_stop ? min(LB_t, VWAP_t) : LB_t). Equities go flat on the last bar of RTH. score_t = pos_t * max(0.2, tanh(|C_t - B_t|/(sigma_j*O_s))), where B_t is UB_t for a long and LB_t for a short. If vwap_only is true: pos_t = sign(C_t - VWAP_t) when |C_t - VWAP_t| > deadzone_atr*ATR14_t, otherwise pos_t = pos_{t-1}; score_t = pos_t*min(1, |C_t - VWAP_t|/ATR14_t).
methods.evidence: This lens has the strongest published evidence. 'Beat the Market' (Zarattini, Aziz, Barbon; SFI WP 24-97) covers SPY from 2007 to early 2024: 1,985% total return net of costs, 19.6% a year, Sharpe 1.33, with the noise area built from a 14-day average absolute move from the open at each time of day, entries checked on the half hour, and a VWAP/boundary trailing stop. It placed 4th at the Quantpedia Awards 2025. 'VWAP: The Holy Grail' (Zarattini and Aziz, 2023) covers QQQ on 1-minute bars from 2018 to 2023: 671% return, Sharpe 2.1, max drawdown 9.4%. Independent QuantConnect replications got much lower numbers ('no holy grail here'). Academic backing: Gao, Han, Li and Zhou (JFE 2018) show the first half-hour return predicts the last half-hour on SPY (1993-2013), more strongly on volatile and high-volume days. Shen, Urquhart and Wang (Financial Review 2022) find the same kind of intraday TSMOM in Bitcoin when sessions are defined by volume. Eross et al. (2019) find BTC volatility and liquidity peak at the major stock-market opens.
methods.caveats: The profits come from a fat right tail on trend days with a low-to-moderate hit rate. Next-5m-bar accuracy may be only about 50-51% even where the strategy pays, so evaluate it with return-weighted, cost-adjusted metrics rather than accuracy alone. The noise area relies on a meaningful session open with an overnight gap (max/min of open and previous close). For crypto the 00:00 UTC open is conventional rather than structural, so the edge should be weaker. Test the us_open anchor. Post-publication decay: Gao et al.'s predictability reportedly declined after 2013. The VWAP holy-grail figures depend on 1-minute granularity and cost assumptions, and replications disagree. The signal persists for many bars, so turnover is low, which is good for surviving costs.

methods.name: Opening-range breakout at session opens
methods.hypothesis: The first 5-30 minutes after a session open (the equity RTH open, or the 00:00 UTC / London / US-open anchors for crypto) set a range. Its direction, or a close outside it, tends to continue, especially when opening volume is unusually high relative to its own history ('stocks in play').
methods.formula: Anchor a: equities 09:30 ET. Crypto uses one of 00:00 UTC, 07:00/08:00 UTC (London, DST-aware), or 13:30/14:30 UTC (US cash open, DST-aware). The OR window is bars [a, a+or_bars-1], with ORH = max H, ORL = min L and ORV = sum V over the window. RVOL = ORV / mean(ORV over the previous 14 sessions at the same anchor). Before the OR completes, score=0. variant='direction' (5m ORB): at e = a+or_bars-1, dir = sign(C_e - O_a) if |C_e - O_a| > 0.05*ATR14_e, else 0; t0 = e. variant='breakout': the first bar t > e and t <= a+48 with C_t > ORH gives dir=+1, or with C_t < ORL gives dir=-1; t0 = t. Stops: with stop='or_opposite', a long stops if C_t < ORL and a short if C_t > ORH. With stop='atr_frac', a long stops if C_t < C_t0 - atr_frac*ATRd14, where ATRd14 is the 14-session mean of the session true range (and mirrored for shorts). After a stop, dir=0 for the rest of the session. g = use_rvol ? clip((RVOL - rvol_min)/(2.0 - rvol_min), 0, 1) : 1. score_t = dir*g*exp(-(t - t0)/decay_bars). The score is 0 after a stop, and at session end for equities.
methods.evidence: Zarattini and Aziz (2023, SSRN 4416622) ran a 5m ORB on QQQ (trade in the direction of the first 5m candle, stop at its extreme, exit EOD): about a 24% hit rate, +0.13R per trade, about 33% a year at 4x leverage. That test charged commissions but no spread or slippage and had no out-of-sample period. An independent replication on five indices found the gross result reproduces but net returns are about zero. Zarattini, Barbon and Aziz ('A Profitable Day Trading Strategy for the U.S. Equity Market', 7,000+ stocks, 2016-2023) find the edge is concentrated in 'stocks in play' (opening-range RVOL >= 100%, top 20): the top-20 portfolio returned 1,600%+ net, Sharpe 2.81. Holmberg, Lonnbark and Lundstrom (Finance Research Letters 2013) report ORB returns and success rates significantly above a fair game on crude oil futures, varying strongly with volatility state. The technique traces back to Crabel (1990). For crypto there are only TradingView implementations; I found no rigorous study.
methods.caveats: The index ORB edge appears to vanish net of realistic costs. Most of the documented edge is single-stock news-driven RVOL, which a single instrument like BTC or SPY lacks; the RVOL gate is the closest analog. Hit rate is low (about 24%), so next-bar directional accuracy is a poor metric for it. Coverage is sparse: one setup per anchor per day. DST handling of anchors must be exact. Off-by-one-hour anchors silently destroy the signal.

methods.name: Bollinger/Keltner squeeze release breakout (TTM-style)
methods.hypothesis: Volatility compression (Bollinger Bands inside Keltner Channels) tends to be followed by expansion. The release direction, taken from a linear-regression momentum oscillator or a band break, predicts the next few bars.
methods.formula: mid_t = SMA_n(C); sd_t = population stdev over n bars of C; BBu = mid + k_bb*sd; BBl = mid - k_bb*sd. KCm = EMA_n(C); KCu = KCm + k_kc*ATR_n; KCl = KCm - k_kc*ATR_n (Wilder ATR). sq_t = (BBu_t < KCu_t) AND (BBl_t > KCl_t). fire_t = sq_{t-1} AND NOT sq_t AND sum_{i=t-n..t-1} sq_i >= min_squeeze_bars. Momentum (LazyBear TTM): y_i = C_i - 0.5*[(HHV_n(H)_i + LLV_n(L)_i)/2 + SMA_n(C)_i]; mom_t is the fitted value at i=t of an OLS line over y_{t-n+1..t}. On fire: dir = sign(mom_t) if dir_mode='momentum'; if dir_mode='band_break', dir = +1 if C_t > BBu_t, -1 if C_t < BBl_t, else 0. Set t_f = t. While t - t_f < 3*decay_bars and sign(mom_t) == dir: score_t = dir*tanh(|mom_t|/(mom_scale_atr*ATR_n,t))*exp(-(t - t_f)/decay_bars). Otherwise score_t = 0. Also export sq_t and bandwidth percentile as regime features.
methods.evidence: Practitioner-only and weak. Backtrex tested a BB squeeze on WTI 4h from 2016 to 2026: +73.7% against +94.6% for buy and hold, 36% win rate, profit factor 1.21, 348 trades. Quantified Strategies reports the squeeze 'doesn't do particularly well for any asset' except perhaps consumer staples (weekly bars). StockCharts (Arthur Hill) tested a squeeze system on S&P 1500 stocks. Crabel's contraction-to-expansion principle is well supported for volatility, but not for direction.
methods.caveats: Compression reliably predicts larger next-bar |return|, but its sign is close to a coin flip. The squeeze state is more valuable as a gate or weighting feature for other directional signals (amplify momentum signals on release, damp reversion signals) than as a direction predictor. Signals are sparse. Low win rate and long-tailed payoffs, as with ORB.

methods.name: Connors RSI(2) / ConnorsRSI / IBS short-term reversion with trend filter
methods.hypothesis: Extreme readings of very short oscillators (RSI(2), ConnorsRSI) and a close at the extreme of the bar's range (Internal Bar Strength) mark short-term overextension that partly reverts on the next bar, preferably in the direction of the longer trend.
methods.formula: RSI_n is Wilder's (RMA of gains/losses, alpha=1/n). X_t = RSI_2(C)_t for variant rsi2. For variant crsi: streak_t = +k after k consecutive higher closes, -k after k lower closes, 0 if unchanged; PR_t = percentage of the last 100 one-bar returns below the current one; X_t = [RSI_3(C)_t + RSI_2(streak)_t + PR_t]/3. Oscillator score (L = lower): r_long = clip((L - X_t)/L, 0, 1); r_short = clip((X_t - (100 - L))/L, 0, 1); s_osc = r_long - r_short. IBS_t = (C_t - L_t)/(H_t - L_t), or 0.5 if H=L. s_ibs = clip((ibs_band - IBS_t)/ibs_band, 0, 1) - clip((IBS_t - (1 - ibs_band))/ibs_band, 0, 1). raw is s_osc for rsi2/crsi, s_ibs for ibs, and clip(0.6*s_osc + 0.4*s_ibs, -1, 1) for rsi2_ibs. Trend filter: tr_t = sign(C_t - SMA_trend_len(C)_t). w = 1 if sign(raw) == tr_t, else counter_trend_weight. score_t = raw*w.
methods.evidence: Connors and Alvarez's RSI(2) (long above the 200-day SMA, enter when RSI2 < 5-10, exit on a close above the 5-day MA) is well documented on daily US index ETFs. The intraday transfer is poor: ProRealCode users testing it on 1m bars called the results 'catastrophic', and the original is explicitly a daily system. Pagonidis' IBS effect (IBS < 0.2 tends to rise the next day, > 0.8 tends to fall) is documented on daily ETFs and corroborated on country ETFs (arXiv 2306.12434). The 5m support is indirect: significant 5m autocorrelation in BTC/ETH markets (arXiv 2003.13517) and anti-correlation at short lags in HF BTC (arXiv 2402.11930). The sign and size are unstable over time, so walk-forward re-estimation matters. A realistic conditional hit rate at extremes is around 51-53%.
methods.caveats: The daily RSI2/IBS edges partly ride equity index drift and overnight-gap effects that do not exist on 5m crypto bars. In trending intraday tape, RSI2 extremes persist. This method is anti-correlated with supertrend, heikin_ashi_trend and noise_area_vwap_trend, which is useful for diversification but means the ensemble must learn regime weights. For SPY/ES, part of the measured reversion is bid-ask bounce in last-trade prices and may not be capturable after the spread. Fees of 2-10 bps often exceed the expected 1-bar reversion size.

methods.name: SuperTrend (ATR trailing-band trend state)
methods.hypothesis: An ATR-banded trailing stop defines the trend state. Being on the bullish side of the SuperTrend line, or having just flipped to it, predicts a slight continuation on the next bar.
methods.formula: hl2 = (H+L)/2; ATR = Wilder ATR(atr_len). bUB_t = hl2_t + mult*ATR_t; bLB_t = hl2_t - mult*ATR_t. fUB_t = bUB_t if (bUB_t < fUB_{t-1} or C_{t-1} > fUB_{t-1}) else fUB_{t-1}. fLB_t = bLB_t if (bLB_t > fLB_{t-1} or C_{t-1} < fLB_{t-1}) else fLB_{t-1}. dir_t = +1 if C_t > fUB_{t-1}; -1 if C_t < fLB_{t-1}; else dir_{t-1}. ST_t = fLB_t if dir_t = +1, else fUB_t. mode='state': score_t = dir_t*[beta + (1 - beta)*tanh(|C_t - ST_t|/(mult*ATR_t))]. mode='flip': score_t = dir_t*exp(-bars_since_flip_t/flip_decay). htf_confirm='1h': compute dir_H on completed 1h bars only (the last 1h bar fully closed at or before t). If dir_H != dir_t, multiply the score by 0.5.
methods.evidence: Default settings are ATR 10 x 3 (Olivier Seban). LiberatedStockTrader's test of 4,052 trades on 30 DJIA stocks: 42-43% win rate, not profitable on daily charts, low expectancy intraday. Quantified Strategies, on 60+ years of the S&P 500, finds it mainly cuts drawdowns rather than adding return. A TradingView BTC 5m SuperTrend script claims a 55% win rate and profit factor 2.2. That claim is unverified, single-sample and filter-heavy, so likely overfit. Related evidence: Corbet et al. (2019) find moving-average rules significant on high-frequency BTC, while Hudson and Urquhart (2021), testing about 15,000 rules with data-snooping controls, find no out-of-sample predictability for Bitcoin.
methods.caveats: In state mode it is mostly a smoothed-momentum sign, highly collinear with heikin_ashi_trend and ema_ribbon_pullback. Cap the combined ensemble weight of trend-state signals. Whipsaw in ranges. Higher-timeframe confirmation must use only completed HTF bars, or it repaints and looks ahead. Low turnover in state mode helps with costs.

methods.name: Heikin-Ashi trend streak
methods.hypothesis: Heikin-Ashi candles smooth noise. A run of same-color HA candles with no opposing wick indicates a persistent short-term trend that slightly favors continuation on the next real bar.
methods.formula: Optional pre-smoothing: O',H',L',C' = EMA_pre_smooth of O,H,L,C (pre_smooth=1 means raw). HAC_t = (O'_t + H'_t + L'_t + C'_t)/4. HAO_t = (HAO_{t-1} + HAC_{t-1})/2, initialized as HAO_0 = (O'_0 + C'_0)/2. HAH_t = max(H'_t, HAO_t, HAC_t); HAL_t = min(L'_t, HAO_t, HAC_t). color_t = sign(HAC_t - HAO_t). streak_t = the number of consecutive bars ending at t with the same color. strong_t = 1 if (color_t = +1 and HAO_t - HAL_t <= wick_eps_atr*ATR14_t) or (color_t = -1 and HAH_t - HAO_t <= wick_eps_atr*ATR14_t), else 0. mode='state': score_t = color_t*min(1, streak_t/n_sat)*((1 - strong_weight) + strong_weight*strong_t). mode='flip': score_t = color_t*exp(-(streak_t - 1)/n_sat), which is strongest on the first bar of a new color. Evaluate against real close-to-close returns, never HA prices.
methods.evidence: Very weak. LiberatedStockTrader's 40-day 5m test pairing ROC with HA candles found a 55% win rate against 45% with standard candles, and reward:risk rising from 1.84 to 2.7. That is a tiny sample with no cost model. TradingView itself warns that strategies run on Heikin-Ashi charts fill at synthetic prices and produce unrealistic results unless 'fill orders using standard OHLC' is enabled. Many published HA 'edges' are this artifact. Mathematically, HA color is roughly the sign of the current OHLC4 minus an EMA of past mid prices, so it is a short EMA-momentum signal.
methods.caveats: The recursive HAO depends on initialization. Warm up for at least 50 bars before scoring. Highly collinear with supertrend, so treat them as one family in the ensemble. Backtests that trade at HA prices are invalid. Always label and score on real closes. Expect at most a tiny next-bar edge; any value is mainly as a regime and persistence feature.

methods.name: NR4/NR7 and inside-bar compression breakout
methods.hypothesis: An unusually narrow bar (the narrowest of the last k bars, optionally also an inside bar) marks coiled supply/demand. A close beyond that bar's range on a following bar tends to start a short directional expansion (Crabel).
methods.formula: R_i = H_i - L_i. NRk_i = (R_i <= min(R_{i-k+1..i})). IB_i = (H_i <= H_{i-1}) AND (L_i >= L_{i-1}). cond_i = NRk_i AND (IB_i if require_inside). Setup bar j = the most recent i in [t - setup_window, t-1] with cond_i true and no breakout yet recorded for j. Breakout at t: up if C_t > H_j + buffer_atr*ATR14_t, down if C_t < L_j - buffer_atr*ATR14_t. Record dir and t_b = t, and mark j as used. score_t = dir*min(1, |C_t - (dir>0 ? H_j : L_j)|/R_j + 0.5)*exp(-(t - t_b)/decay_bars) for t_b <= t < t_b + 3*decay_bars, set to 0 if C_t re-enters [L_j, H_j] (failed breakout). Pending mode (optional): if cond_t is true at bar t itself and no breakout has occurred, score_t = pending_kappa*CLV_t, with CLV_t = (2*C_t - H_t - L_t)/(H_t - L_t).
methods.evidence: Toby Crabel (1990, 'Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout') tabulated NR4, NR7 and ID/NR4 statistics on daily futures; the core finding is contraction followed by expansion. Bulkowski's NR7 statistics on daily stocks show a 46% break-even failure rate on upward breakouts in bull markets. Quantified Strategies reports an NR7 long rule on GLD (daily) with a 71% win rate, +0.3% a trade over 445 trades. One systematic evaluation (arXiv 1812.02527 / oxfordstrat) found NR patterns work better with NR length >= 6 but are not tradeable after costs without additional rules. There is no 5m-specific study.
methods.caveats: On 5m bars, narrow bars cluster in dead hours (Asia-overnight for crypto, lunch for equities) and before holidays, where the follow-through is too small to beat fees. Consider gating by time-of-day volume. The direction comes only from the breakout itself. By the time C_t > H_j, part of the move has already happened. Like squeeze_breakout, it is more reliable as a volatility-expansion feature than as a direction predictor.

methods.name: EMA ribbon pullback / Raschke Holy Grail continuation
methods.hypothesis: In an established short-term trend (fully stacked EMA ribbon, or ADX > 30), a pullback that touches the mid-ribbon EMA and then resumes in the trend direction marks a continuation entry. The next bars favor the trend.
methods.formula: ribbon = [k_1 < k_2 < ... < k_m]; E_k,t = EMA_k(C)_t. Alignment A_t = (1/(m-1))*sum_{i=1..m-1} sign(E_{k_i,t} - E_{k_{i+1},t}), in [-1,1]. variant='ribbon', long trigger at t: A_t >= a_min (a_min = 1.0, fully stacked) AND there exists i in [t - touch_window, t-1] with L_i <= E_pull,i + touch_tol_atr*ATR14_i AND C_t > E_{k_1,t} AND C_t > H_{t-1}. The short trigger mirrors this (A_t <= -a_min, H_i >= E_pull,i - tol, C_t < E_{k_1,t}, C_t < L_{t-1}). At a trigger set t0 = t and dir = sign(A_t). score_t = dir*|A_t|*exp(-(t - t0)/decay_bars) while dir*(C_t - E_pull,t) > 0; otherwise 0. variant='holy_grail': replace the alignment condition with ADX14_t >= adx_min and dir = sign(+DI14 - -DI14), use E_pull = EMA20, and set magnitude = min(1, ADX14_t/50).
methods.evidence: Rules come from Raschke and Connors, 'Street Smarts' (1995): Holy Grail = ADX(14) > 30 and rising, pullback to the 20-period MA, buy above the high of the touch bar. Ribbon pullbacks such as 8/13/21/34/55 are common TradingView scalping tools with no rigorous published backtests that I could find. Moving-average rules on high-frequency BTC were significant in Corbet et al. (2019). Hudson and Urquhart (2021), applying about 15,000 rules with data-snooping corrections, found significant in-sample profitability across cryptocurrencies but none for Bitcoin out of sample.
methods.caveats: Evidence is anecdotal. It is collinear with the supertrend and Heikin-Ashi trend-state family. EMA warm-up needs at least 3x the longest period. Many parameters, so the overfitting risk is high. Keep the grid coarse and shrink toward defaults. The setup is sparse, and the resumption trigger already requires a bar moving in the trend direction, so the residual next-bar edge is small.

methods.name: Three-bar reversal pattern
methods.hypothesis: Two bars in one direction, then a bar that makes the middle bar the swing extreme and closes beyond the prior bar's high (or low), signal exhaustion and a short-term reversal, especially at a stretched location such as an N-bar extreme.
methods.formula: Bullish at t: C_{t-2} < O_{t-2} AND C_{t-1} < O_{t-1} AND L_{t-1} < min(L_{t-2}, L_t) AND C_t > O_t AND C_t > ref, where ref = H_{t-1} if close_ref='prev_high' or H_{t-2} if close_ref='first_high'. All three bars must have nonzero range. Bearish mirrors this: two up bars, H_{t-1} > max(H_{t-2}, H_t), C_t < O_t, C_t < L_{t-1} or L_{t-2}. Location filter (if require_location): bullish requires L_{t-1} == min(L_{t-loc_lookback+1..t}), bearish requires H_{t-1} == max(H over the same window). Volume filter (if vol_confirm): V_t > V_{t-1}. On a pattern set dir and t0 = t. mag = min(1, 0.5 + |C_t - ref|/(gamma_atr*ATR14_t)). score_t = dir*mag*exp(-(t - t0)/decay_bars) for t0 <= t < t0 + 3*decay_bars, and 0 if a newer opposite pattern appears or if C_t breaks back beyond L_{t0-1} (or H_{t0-1}).
methods.evidence: The pattern definition comes from Bulkowski, 'Are Three-Bar Patterns Reliable For Stocks' (S&C, Jan 2000), on daily bars only. Broader candlestick evidence is negative. Marshall, Young and Rose tested 28 candlestick signals on DJIA stocks (1992-2002) with a bootstrap and found 'candlestick technical analysis does not have value'; returns after bullish single-day signals were positive less than half the time. Lo, Mamaysky and Wang (JF 2000) found some kernel-detected daily patterns carry modest incremental information. Nothing rigorous exists at 5m.
methods.caveats: Likely the weakest method on this list. Its main use is as a sparse, low-correlation input that the ensemble may assign zero weight to. By construction bar t already moved strongly in the signal direction, so short-horizon reversion can work against it on t+1. Coverage is low (about 1-3% of bars), so its walk-forward statistics will be noisy. Require minimum event counts before trusting tuned weights.

methodology.topic: Session anchoring for 24/7 crypto vs RTH instruments
methodology.recommendation: Implement a shared anchor utility used by VWAP, noise-area and ORB. Equities/ETFs/ES-RTH anchor at 09:30 America/New_York. Crypto gets three candidate anchors: 00:00 UTC; London 07:00/08:00 UTC; US cash open 13:30/14:30 UTC, all DST-aware via tz conversion, never fixed UTC hours. Make the anchor a tunable parameter. BTC realized volatility and liquidity peak at the major stock-market opens (Eross et al. 2019). Bitcoin intraday momentum is strongest when sessions are defined by volume (Shen, Urquhart and Wang 2022), so the US-open anchor is the most defensible for crypto. Use a rolling 288-bar window as an anchor-free fallback.

methodology.topic: Turning discretionary multi-bar rules into causal next-bar scores
methodology.recommendation: Implement each setup as a causal state machine updated once per closed bar: score = position_direction x confidence x exp(-bars_since_trigger/decay). Return exactly 0 when no setup is active. Persist state across bars (ORB, noise-area, NR breakouts) instead of recomputing from a lookahead window. Report coverage (the fraction of nonzero bars) next to accuracy. The ensemble should weight a sparse signal by its conditional performance times coverage, and must not dilute it by averaging zeros as if they were votes. Any higher-timeframe confirmation (1h SuperTrend, daily ATR) must use only completed HTF bars, to avoid repaint and lookahead.

methodology.topic: Evaluation metrics: accuracy is misleading for breakout systems
methodology.recommendation: Track four things per method and per ensemble: (a) next-bar hit rate on nonzero scores; (b) the return-weighted edge mean(score_t * r_{t+1}) in bps; (c) the cost-adjusted edge mean(score_t*r_{t+1}) - c*mean(|score_t - score_{t-1}|), with c = one-way cost; (d) the information coefficient corr(score_t, r_{t+1}). Breakout/ORB systems are profitable with a hit rate of only about 24% (Zarattini and Aziz QQQ ORB: +0.13R per trade), so a pure directional-accuracy objective will wrongly discard them. Expect realistic next-bar hit rates of 50.5-53% even for the good methods. Typical 5m absolute moves are the same order of magnitude as 2-10 bps round-trip fees, so only high-|score| bars or persistent, low-turnover signals can survive costs.

methodology.topic: Costs, slippage and replication haircut
methodology.recommendation: Charge fees plus a slippage term (at least 1 tick or 1 bp per side) in every walk-forward evaluation, and treat published intraday Sharpe ratios with a large haircut. The 5m ORB paper charged commission but no spread or slippage, and had no out-of-sample test. A five-index replication found 'gross reproduced, net zero'. The QQQ VWAP 'holy grail' (Sharpe 2.1 on 1m bars) came out much lower in public QuantConnect replications. Prefer signals with hysteresis and persistence (noise-area, SuperTrend state) over 1-bar flip signals. Also consider a no-trade band: act only when |ensemble score| exceeds a threshold tuned net of costs.

methodology.topic: Data-snooping control in the daily re-tune
methodology.recommendation: The 10 methods together have hundreds of grid points, so daily re-tuning will find spurious winners. Use: coarse grids (as given); shrinkage toward literature defaults, e.g. choose the best config only if it beats the default by more than 2 standard errors over the trailing window; a stability check that requires neighboring grid points to also be positive; minimum event counts for sparse signals (at least 100 triggers); and a multiple-testing correction (White's Reality Check, Hansen's SPA, or a deflated Sharpe ratio) before increasing a method's ensemble weight. Hudson and Urquhart (2021) found significant in-sample profitability for about 15,000 rules in crypto even after data-snooping controls, but no out-of-sample predictability for Bitcoin. Expect BTC to be the hardest market.

methodology.topic: Regime conditioning and family-level weighting
methodology.recommendation: Group methods into families: trend-state (supertrend, heikin_ashi_trend, ema_ribbon_pullback, noise_area_vwap_trend), breakout (opening_range_breakout, nr_inside_breakout, squeeze_breakout), and reversion (vwap_band_reversion, connors_short_reversion, three_bar_reversal). Cap each family's total weight, because members within a family are highly collinear. Use volatility-compression states (squeeze on/off, NR7, ATR percentile) and time-of-day as gates: amplify momentum and breakout signals on high-volume, high-volatility sessions and after a squeeze releases, and favor reversion in quiet, range-bound hours. This follows Gao et al. (intraday momentum stronger on volatile and high-volume days), Holmberg et al. (ORB returns differ by about 200 bps per day between the highest and lowest volatility states in crude oil), and Crabel's contraction-to-expansion principle.

methodology.topic: Post-publication decay and non-stationarity
methodology.recommendation: Assume published intraday effects decay. Gao et al.'s first-to-last half-hour predictability reportedly weakened after 2013, and BTC rule profitability did not hold out of sample (Hudson and Urquhart). Use trailing walk-forward windows (e.g. 60-120 days of 5m bars for tuning, 5-10 days of purged and embargoed validation) and let ensemble weights decay toward zero when a method's rolling cost-adjusted IC turns negative. Do not hard-code literature parameters as permanent.

methodology.topic: Relative volume as a portable 'stocks in play' filter
methodology.recommendation: The strongest published ORB results depend on relative volume: opening-range volume of at least 100% of its 14-day average, top 20 names. For a single instrument, compute RVOL = opening-range volume / mean opening-range volume at the same anchor over the previous 14 sessions, and use it as a multiplicative gate on breakout and momentum scores. On Binance, the optional taker_buy_base_volume/volume ratio during the opening range can serve as a direction-confirming variant, though that belongs to the order-flow lens.

methodology.topic: Source verification limits
methodology.recommendation: Every page fetch (SSRN, arXiv, RePEc, Concretum, CXO, Backtrex) was blocked by this session's egress proxy, so all evidence and figures here come from search-result abstracts and snippets. Before relying on any specific number (Sharpe, hit rate, return), have a downstream step or a human check the primary PDFs. Treat practitioner/vendor backtests (TradingView, LiberatedStockTrader, Backtrex, Quantified Strategies) as hypothesis sources, not evidence.

methods.name: Online logistic stacker (FTRL-Proximal with shrink-to-prior and forgetting)
methods.hypothesis: The base 5-minute strategy scores are each weak, noisy and non-stationary. A regularized online logistic regression on those scores, pulled toward equal weights and slowly forgetting old data, should give probabilities that are better calibrated and slightly more accurate than any single strategy or a hand-weighted vote. The gain is expected to be small: at most about 0.5-2 percentage points of hit rate and about 1e-4 to 1e-3 nats per bar of log-loss.
methods.formula: Features at bar t: x_t = [1, s_1,t, ..., s_K,t], where each s_k,t in [-1,1] is a base strategy score computed only from bars <= t. Prediction: p_t = sigmoid(w . x_t). Output score_t = clip(2*(0.5 + c*(p_t - 0.5)) - 1, -1, 1), where c is the output shrink in (0,1]. Learning happens one bar late. At the close of bar t, the label for the prediction made at t-1 becomes known: y_t = 1{close[t] > close[t-1]}. Ties are skipped. Gradient: g = (p_{t-1} - y_t) * x_{t-1}. FTRL-Proximal per coordinate i: sigma_i = (sqrt(n_i + g_i^2) - sqrt(n_i)) / alpha; z_i += g_i - sigma_i*w_i; n_i += g_i^2; then w_i = 0 if |z_i| <= l1, else w_i = -(z_i - sign(z_i)*l1) / ((beta + sqrt(n_i))/alpha + l2). To pull weights toward a prior w0 (equal weights 1/K on the scores, 0 on the intercept), run the update on u = w - w0 and add w0 back. Forgetting: once a day, multiply every n_i and z_i by rho = 0.5^(1/H_days). Clip |w_i| <= weight_clip. The daily retune chooses (alpha, l1, l2, H, c) by purged CPCV on the trailing 30 days. It then moves the live hyperparameters only part of the way: new = old + 0.25*(chosen - old).
inputs: base strategy scores s_k,t in [-1,1] (all causal)
optional: 1-2 regime interactions such as s_k,t * vol_z_t, where vol_z_t is a causal EWMA volatility z-score
methods.evidence: FTRL-Proximal with per-coordinate learning rates and elastic-net regularization is the standard production method for streaming logistic regression (McMahan et al., KDD 2013, Google ad-click prediction). In finance, combining forecasts helps out of sample: Rapach, Strauss and Zhou (RFS 2010) found combined forecasts of the equity premium beat the historical average consistently, while individual predictors failed out of sample. The forecast-combination puzzle (Smith and Wallis 2009; Wang et al. 2022 review) shows that estimated weights often lose to equal weights when the true weights are close to equal. That is why the update is regularized toward equal weights. Expected effect at 5 minutes: base strategies near 50.5-52% might combine to 51-53%. The log-loss gain for a calibrated 52% predictor is only about 2*(0.02)^2 = 0.0008 nats per bar.
methods.caveats: Strategy scores that are highly collinear make the individual weights unstable. Keep K at 15 or fewer, or orthogonalize the scores, and rely on the l2 pull toward the prior. The label is only known one bar later, so never update with y_{t+1} before predicting at bar t; check this with a unit test that shifts the labels. A half-life under about 10 days (fewer than about 4,000 effective bars on crypto) chases noise, because detecting 52% vs 50% needs about 3,900 bars. Stacking does not create an edge: if every base score is a coin flip, the stacker converges to p of about 0.5, which is the correct outcome. Watch the calibration slope. A negative slope over the last 3,000 bars means the stacker is anti-predictive and should be rolled back.

methods.name: Fixed-share exponentially weighted forecaster on log-loss with a null expert
methods.hypothesis: Every strategy's would-be prediction is observable on every bar, so this is a full-information experts problem. Exponential weights on log-loss (a Bayesian mixture when eta = 1) with a fixed-share term can track whichever strategy is currently best as regimes change. Its regret against the best expert is guaranteed to be small. Adding a null expert (p = 0.5) lets the ensemble fall back to no signal when nothing works.
methods.formula: Each expert k = 1..K gets a calibrated probability p_k,t = 0.5 + 0.5*a_k*s_k,t, with s_k,t in [-1,1]. The slope a_k comes from a daily Platt fit of y on s_k over the trailing 30 days, is shrunk toward 0, and is clipped to [0, 0.2]. Expert 0 is the null expert, p_0,t = 0.5. After y_t = 1{close[t] > close[t-1]} is observed (ties skipped), compute each expert's loss on its previous prediction: l_k = -[y_t*ln p_k,t-1 + (1-y_t)*ln(1-p_k,t-1)]. Update: v_k = w_k*exp(-eta*l_k); then w_k <- (1-alpha_fs)*v_k/sum_j v_j + alpha_fs/(K+1). Ensemble: p_t = sum_k w_k*p_k,t. Score: score_t = clip((2*p_t - 1)/a_max, -1, 1), with a_max = 0.2. Optional discounted variant: w_k proportional to exp(-eta * sum_s beta^(t-s) * l_k,s), with beta = 0.5^(1/(H_days*bars_per_day)).
inputs: trailing per-expert calibration slopes a_k (refit daily, causal)
methods.evidence: Hedge (Freund and Schapire 1997) with eta = sqrt(8 ln K / T) has regret of at most sqrt((T/2) ln K) for bounded losses. On log-loss, eta = 1 is Vovk's aggregating algorithm, which equals a Bayesian mixture, and its total regret is at most ln(K+1) nats regardless of T. For K = 20 that is about 3.0 nats. For scale, a true 52% expert gains only about 0.0008 nats per bar, or about 6.9 nats over 30 crypto days (8,640 bars). So after a month the mixture keeps roughly half of the best expert's edge. Fixed share (Herbster and Warmuth 1998) gives tracking regret of order sqrt(S*T*log(KT/S)) against the best sequence of experts with S switches. EXP3 and Thompson sampling (Auer et al. 2002; Raj and Kalyani 2017) assume bandit feedback, which this problem does not have, so they would waste information.
methods.caveats: Expert probabilities must be calibrated.
