An uncalibrated expert with p = 0.55/0.45 and a true 52% hit rate has worse log-loss than the null expert (about -0.001 nats per bar), so it would correctly but uselessly lose weight. The regret guarantee is relative to the best expert in hindsight. It cannot tell whether that expert's edge is real or luck, so promotion decisions must still go through the deflated-hurdle and online-FDR gates. With many correlated experts and eta >= 1, weight concentrates on whichever expert got lucky. Prefer eta of 0.25-0.5, fixed share of 1e-4 to 1e-3 per bar, and K of 20 or fewer.

methods.name: Confidence- and cost-gated selective meta-predictor with adaptive coverage
methods.hypothesis: Most 5-minute bars carry essentially no predictable direction, and fees exceed the expected edge on almost all of them. Abstaining (score 0) unless the ensemble is both confident and its expected edge clears costs should raise accuracy on the bars it does predict and make the system economically viable. Coverage is held at a target by an adaptive threshold, so the statistics stay measurable.
methods.formula: Inputs: the ensemble probability p_t from either stacker above, and r_t = ln(C_t/C_{t-1}). Volatility forecast: m_t = EWMA_hl(|r|)_t * tod_t, where tod_t = (median |r| in this 5-minute time-of-day slot over the trailing D days) / (median |r| over all slots in the same D days). Expected edge: E_t = (2*p_t - 1)*m_t. Gate: g_t = 1 if |p_t - 0.5| >= tau_t AND |E_t| >= c_rt + b, otherwise 0. Here c_rt is the round-trip cost in log-return units and b is a buffer. Score: score_t = g_t * clip((2*p_t - 1)/(2*p_cap - 1), -1, 1). Online coverage control (ACI-style): tau_{t+1} = clip(tau_t + gamma*(g_t - c_star), 0, 0.1). Daily reset: set tau to the (1 - c_star) quantile of |p - 0.5| on the trailing validation window. Accept the reset only if the 95% Clopper-Pearson upper bound on selective error over at least 1,000 selected validation bars is below 0.5.
inputs: ensemble probability p_t (from online_logistic_stacker or hedge_fixed_share_ensemble)
instrument round-trip cost c_rt (fees + half-spread*2 + slippage)
methods.evidence: Chow (1970) showed that the Bayes-optimal rejection rule abstains when max(p, 1-p) is below 1 minus the cost of rejecting. Geifman and El-Yaniv (2017) give a selective-guaranteed-risk procedure that picks a threshold so selective error stays at or below a target with probability 1 - delta. Gibbs and Candes (2021) show that the ACI update tau += gamma*(err - target) achieves the long-run target frequency under arbitrary distribution shift. Empirically, a 2026 walk-forward study of hourly BTC-USDT (about 70,000 hours, 27 folds) found that naive sign strategies lost money at 10 bps costs. A filter that trades only when the forecast magnitude exceeds a cost-based threshold restored profitability in some configurations. Jaquart et al. (2021) found 1-60 minute BTC predictability that was profitable before costs but negative after.
methods.caveats: The gate only helps if accuracy actually rises with |p - 0.5|. Check this daily with a reliability or accuracy-by-decile table. Fewer predicted bars means slower validation: at 20% coverage, a 52% edge needs about 19,300 bars (about 67 crypto days, about 250 ES RTH days). At Binance VIP0 taker fees (about 15-20 bps round trip), the cost condition will almost never pass on BTC 5-minute bars, which have E|r| of roughly 8-14 bps. In that case, report realized coverage and flag the instrument as not tradable rather than lowering the cost. The cost condition is a hard constraint, and only tau adapts toward the coverage target. Every component must be causal: the volatility EWMA, the time-of-day medians and tau all use bars <= t only.

methodology.topic: Statistical power: sample sizes and confidence intervals for hit rate
methodology.recommendation: Score models first by calibrated log-loss (or Brier score) against a p = 0.5 baseline. Second, report hit rate on non-tie bars with a Wilson 95% interval. Third, report cost-adjusted PnL. Bars needed to detect a true hit rate vs 50% (one-sided alpha = 0.05, power 0.8): 51% needs 15,454; 52% needs 3,862; 53% needs 1,715; 55% needs 616. Two-sided alpha = 0.05 raises these to 19,620 / 4,903 / 2,178 / 783. Wilson 95% half-width at an observed 52%: n = 1,000 gives ±3.1 pp, 2,000 gives ±2.2 pp, 4,000 gives ±1.55 pp, 10,000 gives ±0.98 pp. The Wilson lower bound first clears 50% at about n = 2,450. In calendar time: crypto has 288 bars a day, so 52% needs about 13.4 days and 51% about 54 days. ES regular trading hours (RTH) have 78 bars a day, so 52% needs about 50 days; ES Globex (about 276 bars a day) needs about 14 days. Divide by coverage when abstaining (20% coverage takes 5x as long). Any rolling window or discount used to estimate skill must have an effective N at or above the required sample: for crypto at 52%, a half-life of at least 10 days (effective N about 4,155 bars). A 5-day half-life gives an effective N of only about 2,078 and chases noise. Exclude ties (close[t+1] == close[t]), which can be several percent of bars for ES, SPY and low-priced alts, and log the tie rate. A true calibrated 52% edge improves log-loss by only about 0.0008 nats per bar.

methodology.topic: Selection-bias hurdle: deflated hit rate and Deflated Sharpe Ratio
methodology.recommendation: Keep a permanent trial registry: every strategy, parameter set and retune ever evaluated, with its out-of-sample series. N is cumulative and never resets. When choosing the best of N candidates, part of the winner's score is luck. The luck hurdle is h*(N, n) = 0.5 + 0.5*E[maxZ_N]/sqrt(n), with E[maxZ_N] = (1-g)*InvPhi(1-1/N) + g*InvPhi(1-1/(N*e)) and g = 0.5772 (Euler-Mascheroni). E[maxZ_N] is 1.58 for N = 10, 2.53 for N = 100, 2.96 for N = 365 and 3.26 for N = 1,000. Example: the best of 100 unskilled configurations over 2,000 bars shows 52.8% by luck alone, and over 5,000 bars 51.8%. Promote only if the observed hit rate exceeds h* and the Wilson lower bound exceeds 0.5. For PnL, compute DSR = Phi[(SR_hat - SR0)*sqrt(T-1)/sqrt(1 - skew*SR_hat + ((kurt-1)/4)*SR_hat^2)], with SR0 = sqrt(Var[SR across trials])*E[maxZ_N]. Use per-bar (not annualized) Sharpe ratios and T in bars. N is the effective number of independent trials: cluster the registry by return correlation, using ONC or counting clusters at correlation above 0.7. Require DSR >= 0.95. Minimum backtest length grows with ln N, so keep each daily grid at 50 configurations or fewer.

methodology.topic: Purged and embargoed walk-forward for the daily retune
methodology.recommendation: Outer loop: true walk-forward on a rolling, not anchored, window. Crypto default is 30 days (8,640 bars) with grid {14, 30, 60, 90} days; ES/SPY default is 60 RTH days (4,680 bars) with grid {40, 60, 120}. Each day, train on [d-W, d-1], predict day d, and use day d for selection only after it has been scored. Inner hyperparameter search: combinatorial purged cross-validation (CPCV) on the training window with 6 contiguous groups and 2 test groups, giving C(6,2) = 15 splits and 5 backtest paths. Purge every training bar whose label interval (t, t+1] overlaps a test bar. Embargo max(1% of T, longest feature lookback, 12) bars after each test block, which is about 86-288 bars for a 30-day window. Fit every normalizer (z-scores, volatility scalers, Platt or isotonic calibrators) inside the training fold only. Rolling estimation windows are also what keep Diebold-Mariano / Giacomini-White model comparisons valid. Use HAC standard errors (Newey-West lag about 12 bars) or a stationary block bootstrap with 1-day blocks to handle volatility clustering.

methodology.topic: Probability of Backtest Overfitting (PBO via CSCV) as a gate on each retune
methodology.recommendation: Each day, build a matrix M of size T x N. Rows are hourly (12-bar) aggregates of out-of-sample log-loss gain or net PnL over the trailing window (30 days gives 720 rows); columns are the N grid configurations. Split the rows into S = 16 contiguous blocks, giving C(16,8) = 12,870 in-sample/out-of-sample splits; if compute is limited, use S = 10 for 252 splits. For each split, take the in-sample best configuration and find its out-of-sample relative rank w in (0,1). Compute logit = ln(w/(1-w)). PBO is the share of splits with logit <= 0. Accept new parameters only if PBO <= 0.25; use 0.10-0.20 for a stricter gate. PBO above 0.5 means the selection procedure is worse than random. Also regress out-of-sample on in-sample performance across splits. A slope at or below zero means the tuning is pure noise, so freeze the parameters and only update the ensemble weights.

methodology.topic: Shrinking parameter and weight updates (pick a plateau, not a peak)
methodology.recommendation: (a) Choose the new parameter value theta* by the neighborhood-smoothed score: the mean over the configuration and its ±1 grid neighbors, not the raw argmax. (b) Move only part of the way: theta_new = theta_old + kappa*(theta* - theta_old), with kappa = 0.25 by default (grid 0.1 / 0.25 / 0.5). Integer lookbacks move at most one grid step per day. (c) If theta* beats theta_old out of sample with a Diebold-Mariano HAC t-statistic below 2, keep theta_old. (d) Ensemble weights: w = (1-lambda)*w_learned + lambda*(1/K), with lambda = 0.5 by default (grid 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75). This follows the forecast-combination puzzle: when the true weights are nearly equal, estimated weights mostly add variance, and equal weights or discounted-MSFE weights (discount 0.9) are hard to beat. (e) Cap any single weight at 0.35. A newly added strategy stays at equal weight until it has at least 4,000 shadow bars.

methodology.topic: Online expert weighting: Hedge with fixed share, not bandits
methodology.recommendation: Every strategy's would-be prediction is observable on every bar, so this is a full-information problem. Use exponential weights on log-loss. Leave EXP3 and Thompson sampling for genuinely scarce slots, such as which candidate gets limited live capital, because bandit algorithms discard counterfactual information and add exploration noise. Settings: eta in {0.25, 0.5, 1}. eta = 1 on log-loss is a Bayesian mixture with total regret of at most ln(K+1), about 3.0 nats for K = 20. Add fixed share alpha in {1e-4, 1e-3} per bar, or discounting with beta = 0.5^(1/(H*288)) and a half-life H of at least 10 days (beta about 0.99976 for crypto). Always include a null expert (p = 0.5). Scale check: a true 52% expert earns only about 0.0008 nats per bar, about 6.9 nats per 30 crypto days, so the regret allowance alone can absorb half the edge in a month. In hit-rate terms, Hedge's sqrt((T/2) ln K) bound for K = 20 over 8,640 bars is about 1.3 percentage points per bar, the same size as the edge being sought. Hedge ensures you are not much worse than the best expert but cannot certify that the best expert is real. If Thompson sampling is used for promotion slots, use Beta(1 + discounted hits, 1 + discounted misses) with a per-bar discount of 0.9998 (half-life about 12 days).

methodology.topic: Multiple testing when a new strategy is tested every day
methodology.recommendation: Treat each daily candidate as one hypothesis in an online false-discovery-rate (FDR) procedure. Get its p-value from a one-sided HAC Diebold-Mariano test (Newey-West lag 12 bars, or a block bootstrap with 1-day blocks). The test compares log-loss of the ensemble with the candidate added against the incumbent ensemble, over a forward shadow period of at least 4,000 bars (about 14 crypto days, about 50 ES RTH days) that was not used to design the candidate. Accept with LORD++ at FDR q = 0.10, or with alpha-investing at initial wealth 0.05 and payout 0.05. Simpler fallback: require t >= 3.0 on the shadow-period loss differential (the Harvey-Liu-Zhu hurdle, which corresponds to roughly FDR <= 5%). When the whole roster is compared against a benchmark at once, use Hansen's SPA test or Romano-Wolf StepM (both bootstrap). Use the Model Confidence Set to decide which strategies are statistically indistinguishable from the best. Count every candidate in the registry N used by the deflated Sharpe ratio, whether it passed or failed.

methodology.topic: Anytime-valid monitoring (the loop checks results every day)
methodology.recommendation: Re-running a fixed-sample test every day inflates false positives. In a simulation with true p = 0.5 and 288 bars a day, a one-sided 5% z-test checked daily falsely declared an edge in 23.6% of runs within 30 days and 30.4% within 90 days. Use a betting test martingale instead: K_t = product over predicted non-tie bars of (1 + lambda*(2*x_i - 1)), where x_i = 1 if correct. Set lambda = 2*(p1 - 0.5) = 0.04 for the alternative p1 = 0.52, or adapt lambda_t in [0, 0.1] using only past data. Declare an edge when K_t >= 1/alpha = 20; Ville's inequality bounds the false-alarm probability at 5% no matter how often you look. If the true rate is 52%, expect about ln(20)/0.0008, roughly 3,750 bars. For a two-sided decision, Wald's SPRT of p = 0.50 vs p = 0.52 (alpha = 0.05, beta = 0.2) uses log-likelihood-ratio bounds of +2.77 and -1.56, adds +0.0392 per hit and -0.0408 per miss, and needs on average about 2,380 bars under the alternative and about 1,680 under the null, about 40% fewer than the fixed-sample 3,862. Report confidence sequences instead of fixed confidence intervals on dashboards.

methodology.topic: Champion/challenger with automatic rollback rules
methodology.recommendation: Keep the last 5 known-good parameter and weight versions. Always run in shadow: the current champion, the previous champion, an equal-weight ensemble and the null expert (no trade). Roll back on any of these triggers: (i) over the trailing 864 bars (3 crypto days; 10 days for ES RTH), a Diebold-Mariano test of champion vs previous champion log-loss gives t < -2.0; (ii) a Bernoulli CUSUM on misses, S_t = max(0, S_{t-1} + miss_t - 0.495), alarms at h = 25. In simulation, this alarms after about 9,750 predicted bars on average when the true hit rate is 52%, after about 1,990 bars if it falls to 50%, about 1,190 at 49% and about 590 at 47%. (iii) The Wilson 95% upper bound of hit rate over the last 2,000 predicted bars falls below 0.50. (iv) Realized net drawdown exceeds 3x the backtest's 95th-percentile daily drawdown. (v) The calibration slope over the last 3,000 bars is below 0. The ladder: roll back to the previous champion. If it also fails trigger (iii), fall back to equal weights. If equal weights also fail, abstain on every bar until the test martingale crosses 20 again. ADWIN or Page-Hinkley on per-bar log-loss are drop-in alternatives to the CUSUM. Log every rollback as a trial.

methodology.topic: Abstention with coverage constraints (selective prediction)
methodology.recommendation: Predict only when |p - 0.5| >= tau_t AND (2p - 1)*E_t|r| >= c_rt + buffer. E_t|r| is a causal EWMA of |r| with a 24-bar half-life, times a time-of-day factor. Target coverage c* = 20%, allowed band 10-40%. Set tau each day as the (1 - c*) quantile of |p - 0.5| on validation data, then adapt it online with tau_{t+1} = tau_t + 0.005*(predicted_t - c*), clamped to [0, 0.1]. Accept a threshold only if the 95% Clopper-Pearson upper bound on selective error, over at least 1,000 selected validation bars, is below 0.5; this is the Geifman-El-Yaniv selective-risk guarantee with delta = 0.05. Never let the coverage target override the cost condition. If realized coverage is below 5% for 5 days, flag the instrument as not tradable at its current costs. Note the cost in sample size: at 20% coverage, confirming 52% takes about 19,300 bars (about 67 crypto days or about 250 ES RTH days). Below 10% coverage, daily statistics are meaningless.

methodology.topic: Cost reality check: break-even hit rate
methodology.recommendation: If each prediction is a round trip (enter at close t, exit at close t+1) and move size is independent of being right, the break-even hit rate is p_be = 0.5 + c/(2*E|r|). Measure E|r| causally per instrument. BTC 5-minute E|r| is roughly 8-14 bps. At c = 10 bps, p_be is about 0.86-1.0, which is unreachable. Binance VIP0 is 0.10% per side, so 20 bps round trip, or 15 bps with the BNB discount. At c = 2 bps (high VIP tier or maker fills), p_be is about 0.57-0.62. ES costs about 0.5-1 bp round trip against an E|r| of about 4-8 bps, so p_be is about 0.55-0.60. SPY at about 0.2-0.5 bp gives about 0.52-0.55, the only setting where a 52-53% edge could plausibly pay. Therefore: train and tune on log-loss and hit rate, but trade only when the cost gate passes; stay in the position through consecutive same-sign predictions and pay costs only on flips; always report PnL net of fees, 2x half-spread and slippage. Literature: Jaquart et al. (2021) found 1-60 minute BTC predictability above random, with gross monthly returns up to 39% that turned negative after costs. A 2026 hourly BTC-USDT walk-forward study found naive sign trading fails at 10 bps, and a cost-threshold filter rescued only some configurations. A 54% figure for 5-minute MLP direction accuracy should be treated as optimistic and likely affected by selection.

methodology.topic: Probability calibration and output shrinkage
methodology.recommendation: Turn every strategy score and the ensemble score into a probability with Platt scaling, p = sigmoid(a + b*score), fit each day on the trailing 20-30 days with purging. For liquid instruments at 5 minutes, clip p to [0.40, 0.60]; calibrated probabilities outside that range almost always mean overfitting or leakage. Monitor expected calibration error (10 bins) and the calibration slope b. A healthy b is 0.5-1.5; b <= 0 triggers rollback. Shrink p' = 0.5 + s*(p - 0.5), with s fitted daily, and default to s = 0.5 when the shadow sample is below about 4,000 bars. Emit score = 2*p' - 1 in [-1, 1]. Use log-loss and Brier score, both proper scoring rules, for every weighting and promotion decision. Hit rate rewards overconfident models and wastes information.
